title.zh: 卷一百零八 列傳第三十三 劉仁軌 裴行儉子:光庭 稹 玄孫:均 婁師德
title.en: Volume 108 Biographies 33: Liu Rengui, Pei Xingjian and Sons: Guang Ting, Zhen, Great-great-grandson: Jun, Lou Shide
title.raw: 卷一百零八 列傳第三十三 劉仁軌 裴行儉子:光庭 稹 玄孫:均 婁師德 Volume 108 Biographies 33: Liu Rengui, Pei Xingjian and Sons: Guang Ting, Zhen, Great-great-grandson: Jun, Lou Shide

sentences.zh: 劉仁軌 裴行儉子:光庭 稹 玄孫:均 婁師德

translations.literal: Liu Rengui; Pei Xingjian, sons: Guangting, Zhen; great-great-grandson: Jun; Lou Shide.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Rengui; Pei Xingjian, with his sons Guangting and Zhen; his great-great-grandson Jun; and Lou Shide.

sentences.zh: 劉仁軌

translations.literal: Liu Rengui.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Rengui.

sentences.zh: 劉仁軌，字正則，汴州尉氏人。

translations.literal: Liu Rengui, styled Zhengze, was a native of Weishi in Bian Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Rengui, courtesy name Zhengze, came from Weishi County in Bianzhou.

sentences.zh: 少貧賤，好學。

translations.literal: In youth he was poor and lowly, and fond of learning.
translations.idiomatic: As a young man he was poor and of humble status, yet devoted to study.

sentences.zh: 值亂，不能安業，每動止，畫地書空，寓所習，卒以通博聞。

translations.literal: Encountering disorder, he could not settle to his work; with every movement and pause he would draw on the ground or write in the air, lodging what he had learned, and in the end became widely known for broad learning.
translations.idiomatic: Turmoil made steady work impossible; wherever he went he traced characters on the ground or wrote in the air, rehearsing what he had studied until his wide learning became renowned.

sentences.zh: 武德初，河南道安撫大使任瑰上疏有所論奏，仁軌見其稿，為竄定數言。

translations.literal: In the early Wude era, Ren Gui, the Henan Circuit pacification commissioner, submitted a memorial discussing certain matters; Rengui saw the draft and revised several phrases for him.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Wude reign, Ren Gui, commissioner for pacifying Henan Circuit, was drafting a memorial on state affairs; Rengui read it and corrected several passages.

sentences.zh: 瑰驚異，赤牒補息州參軍。

translations.literal: Gui was astonished and, by informal red commission, appointed him acting staff officer of Xi Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Ren Gui was impressed and used an informal red-ink appointment to make him a staff officer in Xi Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 轉陳倉尉。

translations.literal: He was transferred to be sheriff of Chencang.
translations.idiomatic: He was next posted as sheriff of Chencang County.

sentences.zh: 部人折沖都尉魯寧者，豪縱犯法，縣莫敢屈。

translations.literal: Among those under his jurisdiction was Zhechong colonel Lu Ning, who was arrogant and unrestrained and broke the law; no one in the county dared restrain him.
translations.idiomatic: His jurisdiction included Zhechong colonel Lu Ning, a man so arrogant and lawless that the county authorities dared not bring him to heel.

sentences.zh: 仁軌約不再犯，而甯暴橫自如，仁軌搒殺之。

translations.literal: Rengui bound him not to offend again, but Ning was violent and overbearing as before, so Rengui had him flogged to death.
translations.idiomatic: Rengui made Lu Ning promise not to offend again, yet Ning continued his tyrannical ways; Rengui had him beaten to death.

sentences.zh: 州以聞，太宗曰：「尉而殺吾折沖，可乎？」

translations.literal: The prefecture reported it, and Emperor Taizong said, "Is it permissible for a sheriff to kill my Zhechong colonel?
translations.idiomatic: When the prefecture reported the matter, Emperor Taizong asked, "May a county sheriff kill one of my Zhechong colonels?

sentences.zh: 召詰讓。

translations.literal: He summoned and reprimanded him.
translations.idiomatic: He had Rengui summoned and upbraided him.

sentences.zh: 仁軌對曰：「寧辱臣，臣故殺之。」

translations.literal: Rengui replied, "Because Ning insulted me, I therefore killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Rengui answered, "He insulted me, and that is why I killed him.

sentences.zh: 帝以為剛正，更擢咸陽丞。

translations.literal: The emperor considered him upright and firm, and further promoted him to assistant magistrate of Xianyang.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor admired his firm integrity and promoted him to assistant magistrate of Xianyang.

sentences.zh: 貞觀十四年，校獵同州。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Zhenguan, the emperor hunted at Tong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In 640, the emperor went hunting in Tongzhou.

sentences.zh: 時秋斂未訖，仁軌諫曰：「今茲澍澤沾足，百穀熾茂，收才十二。

translations.literal: The autumn harvest was not yet finished; Rengui remonstrated, saying, "This year timely rains have been ample, the hundred grains flourish luxuriantly, and scarcely one or two tenths have been gathered in.
translations.idiomatic: With the autumn harvest still unfinished, Rengui admonished the emperor: "This year's rains have been abundant and the crops are luxuriant, yet only a tenth or two has been reaped.

sentences.zh: 常日贅調，已有所妨。

translations.literal: Even on ordinary days the supplemental levies already cause hindrance.
translations.idiomatic: Even routine corvée levies already burden the farmers.

sentences.zh: 又供獵事，繕橋治道，役雖簡省，猶不損數萬。

translations.literal: Now, in addition, to supply the hunt, repair bridges and roads—the labor, though simplified, still comes to no less than tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Hunting preparations—repairing bridges and roads—will require tens of thousands of laborers even if kept to a minimum.

sentences.zh: 少延一旬，使場圃畢勞，陛下六飛徐驅，公私交泰。」

translations.literal: If You delay a brief ten days so that threshing floors and gardens finish their toil, Your Majesty's six-horse chariot may drive slowly, and public and private affairs will both prosper.
translations.idiomatic: Delay ten days until harvesting is complete, and Your Majesty may advance at leisure with public and private interests alike secure.

sentences.zh: 璽書褒納。

translations.literal: An imperial sealed letter praised and accepted his advice.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied with a sealed edict commending and accepting his counsel.

sentences.zh: 拜新安令。

translations.literal: He was appointed magistrate of Xin'an.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed magistrate of Xin'an County.

sentences.zh: 累遷給事中。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to supervising secretary.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through successive posts to supervising secretary in the palace secretariat.

sentences.zh: 為李義府所惡，出為青州刺史。

translations.literal: Detested by Li Yifu, he was sent out as prefect of Qingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yifu turned against him, and he was transferred to serve as prefect of Qingzhou.

sentences.zh: 顯慶五年，伐遼，義府欲斥以罪，使督漕，而船果覆沒。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Xianqing, during the campaign against Liaodong, Yifu wishing to drive him off with a charge had him supervise grain transport, and the ships indeed capsized and sank.
translations.idiomatic: In 660, during the Liaodong campaign, Li Yifu sought to ruin him by assigning him to oversee shipping; the convoy duly foundered.

sentences.zh: 坐免官，白衣隨軍。

translations.literal: For this he was dismissed from office and followed the army in plain clothes.
translations.idiomatic: Stripped of rank, he accompanied the army as a civilian appointee.

sentences.zh: 初，蘇定方既平百濟，留郎將劉仁願守其城，左衛中郎將王文度為熊津都督，撫納殘黨。

translations.literal: At first, after Su Dingfang had pacified Baekje, he left regimental commander Liu Renyuan to hold its capital, and Left Guard mid-ranking general Wang Wendu served as commissioner of Xiongjin to soothe and receive the remnant factions.
translations.idiomatic: When Su Dingfang first conquered Baekje, he left regimental commander Liu Renyuan to hold the capital and assigned Left Guard general Wang Wendu as Xiongjin commissioner to pacify the surviving loyalists.

sentences.zh: 文度死，百濟故將福信及浮屠道琛迎故王子扶余豐立之，引兵圍仁願。

translations.literal: Wendu died; Baekje's former general Fuxin and the monk Daochen welcomed the former prince Buyeo Pung and enthroned him, leading troops to besiege Renyuan.
translations.idiomatic: After Wang Wendu died, the former Baekje general Fuxin and the monk Daochen restored Buyeo Pung as king and laid siege to Liu Renyuan.

sentences.zh: 詔仁軌檢校帶方州刺史，統文度之眾，併發新羅兵為援，仁軌將兵嚴整，轉鬥陷陣，所向無前。

translations.literal: An edict made Rengui acting prefect of Daifang and put him in command of Wendu's troops, also dispatching Silla forces as reinforcements; Rengui's army was strict and ordered, fighting in rotation to break formations, and wherever they turned none could stop them.
translations.idiomatic: Rengui was ordered to serve as acting Daifang prefect, take over Wang Wendu's command, and march with Silla reinforcements; his troops fought in tight order and broke every line they faced.

sentences.zh: 信等釋仁願圍，退保任存城。

translations.literal: Fuxin and the others lifted the siege on Renyuan and withdrew to hold Rencun Fort.
translations.idiomatic: Fuxin's forces abandoned the siege and fell back to Rencun Fort.

sentences.zh: 既而福信殺道琛，並其眾，招還叛亡，勢張甚。

translations.literal: Soon after, Fuxin killed Daochen, absorbed his followers, and summoned back deserters and fugitives; their power grew greatly.
translations.idiomatic: Fuxin then killed Daochen, absorbed his men, rallied deserters, and swelled his power considerably.

sentences.zh: 仁軌與仁願合，則解甲休士。

translations.literal: When Rengui joined Renyuan, they doffed armor and rested the troops.
translations.idiomatic: Rengui and Renyuan united their forces and gave the men rest.

sentences.zh: 時定方伐高麗，圍平壤不克。

translations.literal: At that time Dingfang was campaigning against Goguryeo and besieged Pyongyang without success.
translations.idiomatic: Meanwhile Su Dingfang besieged Pyongyang in his Goguryeo campaign but failed to take it.

sentences.zh: 高宗詔仁軌拔軍就新羅與金法敏議去留計。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozong ordered Rengui to withdraw the army, join Silla, and consult with Kim Beopmin on whether to stay or leave.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozong instructed Rengui to pull back to Silla and consult Kim Beopmin on whether to remain or withdraw.

sentences.zh: 將士鹹欲還，仁軌曰：「《春秋》之義，大夫出強，有可以安社稷、便國家者，得專之。

translations.literal: The officers and soldiers all wished to return; Rengui said, "The meaning of the Spring and Autumn Annals is that when a high official goes abroad, if something can secure the altars of state and benefit the realm, he may decide it on his own.
translations.idiomatic: The troops wanted to go home, but Rengui argued: "Spring and Autumn teaches that a minister abroad may act on his own authority when the altars of state and national interest require it.

sentences.zh: 今天子欲滅高麗，先誅百濟，留兵鎮守，制其心腹。

translations.literal: Now the Son of Heaven wishes to destroy Goguryeo; he first executed Baekje and left troops to garrison and control its heartland.
translations.idiomatic: His Majesty intends to destroy Goguryeo by first crushing Baekje and garrisoning its heartland.

sentences.zh: 雖孽豎跳樑，士力未完，宜厲兵粟馬，乘無備，擊不意，百不百全。

translations.literal: Though wicked brats leap on the beams and troop strength is not yet complete, one should sharpen weapons and ready grain and horses, strike when they are unprepared and hit them unawares—though not perfectly assured of success.
translations.idiomatic: Though rebel chieftains are still active and our strength incomplete, we should arm and provision the army, catch them off guard, and strike—even if victory is not absolutely guaranteed.

sentences.zh: 戰勝之日，開張形勢，騰檄濟師，聲援接，虜亡矣。

translations.literal: On the day of victory, expand the military posture, dispatch urgent dispatches to ferry reinforcements, and when supporting voices connect, the foe will perish.
translations.idiomatic: After victory we can expand our position, send urgent appeals for reinforcements, and when relief arrives the enemy will be finished.

sentences.zh: 今平壤不勝，熊津又拔，則百濟之燼復炎，高麗之滅無期。

translations.literal: If Pyongyang is not taken and Xiongjin is also withdrawn, then Baekje's embers will blaze again and Goguryeo's destruction will have no term.
translations.idiomatic: If Pyongyang fails while we abandon Xiongjin, Baekje's embers will flare up again and Goguryeo will never be conquered.

sentences.zh: 吾等雖入新羅，正似坐客，有不如志，悔可得邪？

translations.literal: Even if we enter Silla, it will be exactly like sitting as guests; should things not go as wished, can regret be recovered?
translations.idiomatic: Withdraw into Silla and we become mere guests; if things go wrong, regret will come too late.

sentences.zh: 扶余豐猜貳，表合內攜，熱不支久。

translations.literal: Buyeo Pung is suspicious and divided; outwardly united but inwardly at odds—such heat cannot last long.
translations.idiomatic: Buyeo Pung is suspicious and duplicitous; their outward alliance hides inner quarrels and cannot endure.

sentences.zh: 宜堅守伺變以圖之，不可輕動。」

translations.literal: One ought to hold firm, watch for changes, and seek advantage; one must not move lightly.
translations.idiomatic: We should hold fast, watch for openings, and strike only when the moment is right—not act rashly.

sentences.zh: 眾從其議，乃請益兵。

translations.literal: The multitude followed his plan and then requested additional troops.
translations.idiomatic: The assembly agreed and petitioned for reinforcements.

sentences.zh: 時賊守真峴城，仁軌夜督新羅兵薄城扳堞，比明，入之，遂通新羅饟道。

translations.literal: At that time the rebels held Zhenxian Fort; Rengui by night directed Silla troops to press the walls and scale the parapets, and by dawn they entered it, thus opening Silla's supply route.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels held Zhenxian Fort; Rengui led Silla troops in a night assault up the walls and took it by dawn, securing the Silla supply line.

sentences.zh: 而豐果襲殺福信，遣使至高麗、倭丐援。

translations.literal: And Pung indeed launched a surprise attack and killed Fuxin, sending envoys to Goguryeo and Wa to beg for aid.
translations.idiomatic: Buyeo Pung duly ambushed and killed Fuxin, then sent envoys to Goguryeo and Japan begging for help.

sentences.zh: 會詔遣右威衛將軍孫仁師率軍浮海而至，士氣振。

translations.literal: It happened that an edict dispatched Right Might Guard general Sun Renshi to lead troops by sea, and morale revived.
translations.idiomatic: An imperial order then brought Right Might Guard general Sun Renshi across the sea with reinforcements, and spirits soared.

sentences.zh: 於是，諸將議所向，或曰：「加林城水陸之沖，盍先擊之？」

translations.literal: Thereupon the generals debated where to strike; someone said, "Jialin Fort is the crossroads of land and water—why not attack it first?
translations.idiomatic: The commanders debated their next target; some urged striking Jialin Fort first, the junction of land and sea routes.

sentences.zh: 仁軌曰：「兵法避實擊虛。

translations.literal: Rengui said, "The art of war is to avoid the solid and strike the empty.
translations.idiomatic: Rengui replied, "Strategy teaches us to avoid the strong point and strike the weak.

sentences.zh: 加林險而固，攻則傷士，守則曠日。

translations.literal: Jialin is perilous and firm; to attack will wound soldiers, to besiege will waste days.
translations.idiomatic: Jialin is steep and fortified—assault would cost men, siege would waste time.

sentences.zh: 周留城，賊巢穴，群凶聚焉。

translations.literal: Zhouliu Fort is the rebels' nest, where the wicked gather.
translations.idiomatic: Zhouliu is the rebel stronghold where their leaders have assembled.

sentences.zh: 若克之，諸城自下。」

translations.literal: If it is taken, the other forts will submit of themselves."
translations.idiomatic: Capture Zhouliu and the rest will fall of their own accord."

sentences.zh: 於是仁師、仁願及法敏帥陸軍以進，仁軌與杜爽、扶余隆繇熊津白江會之。

translations.literal: Thereupon Renshi, Renyuan, and Beopmin led the land army forward; Rengui with Du Shuang and Buyeo Yung went by Xiongjin and the Ba River to join them.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Renshi, Liu Renyuan, and Kim Beopmin advanced overland while Rengui, Du Shuang, and Buyeo Yung sailed from Xiongjin up the Ba River to rendezvous.

sentences.zh: 遇倭人白江口，四戰皆克，焚四百艘，海水為丹。

translations.literal: They met the Wa people at the mouth of the Ba River; in four battles all were victories, four hundred ships were burned, and the sea water turned red.
translations.idiomatic: At the mouth of the Ba River they met the Japanese fleet, won four engagements, burned four hundred ships, and turned the sea crimson.

sentences.zh: 扶余豐脫身走，獲其寶劍。

translations.literal: Buyeo Pung escaped with his life and fled; his treasured sword was captured.
translations.idiomatic: Buyeo Pung fled for his life, leaving his jeweled sword behind as spoils.

sentences.zh: 偽王子扶余忠勝、忠志等率其眾與倭人降，獨酋帥遲受信據任存城未下。

translations.literal: The pretender princes Buyeo Zhongsheng, Zhongzhi, and others led their followers and the Wa to surrender; only the chieftain Chi Shouxin held Rencun Fort and would not yield.
translations.idiomatic: The princes Buyeo Zhongsheng and Zhongzhi surrendered with their followers and the Japanese; only the chieftain Chi Shouxin still held out at Rencun Fort.

sentences.zh: 始，定方破百濟，酋領沙吒相如、黑齒常之嘯亡散，據險以應福信，至是皆降。

translations.literal: At the outset, when Dingfang conquered Baekje, the chieftains Shazha Xiangru and Heichi Changzhi had gathered scattered fugitives and held perilous places to respond to Fuxin; by this time all surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: After Su Dingfang's conquest, the chieftains Shazha Xiangru and Heichi Changzhi had rallied scattered rebels in the hills to support Fuxin; now they all submitted.

sentences.zh: 仁軌以赤心示之，畀取任存自效，即給鎧仗糧Я。

translations.literal: Rengui showed them his sincere heart, set them to take Rencun to prove themselves, and at once gave them armor, weapons, and grain and supplies.
translations.idiomatic: Rengui pledged his trust, sent them to retake Rencun Fort on their own merit, and promptly furnished them with armor, weapons, and rations.

sentences.zh: 仁師曰：「夷狄野心難信，若受甲濟粟，資寇便也。」

translations.literal: Renshi said, "Barbarians' savage hearts are hard to trust; if they receive armor and supplied grain, it is arming the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Renshi objected: "These frontier peoples are treacherous—give them arms and grain and we merely arm our enemies.

sentences.zh: 仁軌曰：「吾觀相如、常之忠而謀，因機立功，尚何疑？」

translations.literal: Rengui said, "I observe that Xiangru and Changzhi are loyal and resourceful; to seize the occasion and achieve merit—why still doubt?"
translations.idiomatic: Rengui answered, "Xiangru and Changzhi are loyal and capable; this is their chance to distinguish themselves—why hesitate?"

sentences.zh: 二人訖拔其城。

translations.literal: The two men in the end captured the fort.
translations.idiomatic: The two men duly captured the fort.

sentences.zh: 遲受信委妻子奔高麗，百濟餘黨悉平。

translations.literal: Chi Shouxin abandoned his wife and children and fled toward Goguryeo; Baekje's remaining factions were all pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Chi Shouxin abandoned his family and fled to Goguryeo, and the last Baekje resistance was eliminated.

sentences.zh: 仁師等振旅還，詔留仁軌統兵鎮守。

translations.literal: Renshi and the others returned with troops in good order; an edict ordered Rengui to remain and command the garrison.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Renshi departed with his army while Rengui was ordered to stay behind in command.

sentences.zh: 百濟再被亂，僵屍如莽，仁軌始命瘞埋弔祭焉。

translations.literal: Baekje had twice suffered turmoil; corpses lay like brushwood; Rengui first ordered burial and mourning sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: After two rounds of upheaval, Baekje was littered with unburied dead; Rengui ordered their proper burial and memorial rites.

sentences.zh: 葺復戶版，署官吏，開道路，營聚落，復防堰，賑貧貸乏，勸課耕種，為立官社，民皆安其所。

translations.literal: He restored household registers, appointed officials, opened roads, established settlements, repaired dikes and barrages, relieved the poor and lent to the destitute, urged farming and taxation, established official altars of soil and grain, and the people all found peace in their places.
translations.idiomatic: He restored census records and local administration, rebuilt roads and villages, repaired dikes, aided the poor, promoted agriculture, and established official altars—the people at last had secure livelihoods.

sentences.zh: 遂營屯田，以經略高麗。

translations.literal: Thereupon he established garrison farming to plan the conquest of Goguryeo.
translations.idiomatic: He then organized garrison farms to prepare for operations against Goguryeo.

sentences.zh: 仁願至京師，帝勞曰：「若本武將，軍中奏請，皆有文理，何道而然？」

translations.literal: When Renyuan reached the capital, the emperor comforted him, saying, "You were originally a military general; your military memorials all have literary order—by what method is this so?
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Renyuan reached the capital, the emperor asked how a career soldier could write such polished memorials from the field.

sentences.zh: 對曰：「仁軌之辭，非臣所能。」

translations.literal: He replied, "Rengui's phrasing is beyond what this subject can match."
translations.idiomatic: Renyuan replied that the words were Liu Rengui's, not his own.

sentences.zh: 帝歎賞之，超進仁軌六階，真拜帶方州刺史，賜第一區，厚賚妻子，璽書褒勉。

translations.literal: The emperor sighed in appreciation, promoted Rengui six ranks in excess of the norm, formally appointed him prefect of Daifang, granted one prime residence, richly rewarded his wife and children, and sent a sealed letter of commendation and encouragement.
translations.idiomatic: Deeply impressed, the emperor promoted Rengui six steps above the norm, confirmed him as Daifang prefect, granted a capital residence and generous rewards for his family, and sent a sealed letter of praise.

sentences.zh: 先是，貞觀、永徽中，士戰歿者皆詔使弔祭，或以贈官推授子弟。

translations.literal: Previously, in the Zhenguan and Yonghui eras, soldiers who died in battle all had imperial envoys sent to mourn and sacrifice, or posthumous offices granted or transferred to sons and younger kinsmen.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhenguan and Yonghui reigns, soldiers killed in action were mourned by imperial envoys and their sons often received posthumous honors.

sentences.zh: 顯慶後，討伐恩賞殆絕；

translations.literal: After Xianqing, rewards for campaigns and conquest nearly ceased.
translations.idiomatic: After the Xianqing era, campaign rewards all but disappeared.

sentences.zh: 及破百濟、平壤，有功者皆不甄敘。

translations.literal: When Baekje and Pyongyang were taken, those with merit were none recorded or ranked.
translations.idiomatic: Veterans of the Baekje and Pyongyang campaigns received no recognition of their service.

sentences.zh: 州縣購募，不願行，身壯家富者，以財參逐，率得避免。

translations.literal: When prefectures and counties conscripted recruits, men did not wish to go; those young and strong or rich used bribes to chase officials away and mostly escaped.
translations.idiomatic: Conscription notices met widespread reluctance; young, wealthy men bribed their way out and usually escaped service.

sentences.zh: 所募皆佇劣寒憊，無鬥志。

translations.literal: Those recruited were all sluggish, inferior, cold, and weary, with no will to fight.
translations.idiomatic: Those who were pressed into service were the weak, the poor, and the dispirited—men with no stomach for battle.

sentences.zh: 仁軌具論其弊，請加慰賚，以鼓士心。

translations.literal: Rengui fully set forth these abuses and requested added comfort and rewards to rouse soldiers' hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Rengui catalogued these abuses and petitioned for better rewards to restore military morale.

sentences.zh: 又表用扶餘隆，使綏定餘眾。

translations.literal: He also memorialized to employ Buyeo Yung to soothe and settle the remaining multitude.
translations.idiomatic: He also recommended Buyeo Yung to pacify the remaining Baekje population.

sentences.zh: 帝乃以隆為熊津都督。

translations.literal: The emperor then made Yung commissioner of Xiongjin.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor appointed Buyeo Yung Xiongjin commissioner.

sentences.zh: 時劉仁願為卑列道總管，詔率兵度海，使代舊屯，與仁軌俱還。

translations.literal: At that time Liu Renyuan was grand commander of the Beilie Circuit; an edict ordered him to lead troops across the sea, replace the old garrison, and return together with Rengui.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Renyuan, overall commander of the Beilie Circuit, was ordered to cross the sea with fresh troops, relieve the garrison, and bring Rengui home.

sentences.zh: 仁軌曰：「上巡狩方嶽，又經略高麗。

translations.literal: Rengui said, "Above, the emperor is touring the sacred peaks and also planning Goguryeo.
translations.idiomatic: Rengui objected: "The emperor is touring the sacred mountains while still planning war against Goguryeo.

sentences.zh: 方農時，而吏與兵悉被代，新至者未習，萬一蠻夷生變，誰與捍之？

translations.literal: It is just farming season, yet officers and soldiers are all replaced; the newly arrived are untrained—if barbarians should suddenly rise in turmoil, with whom will one defend?
translations.idiomatic: It is planting season, yet every officer and soldier is being rotated out; the replacements are untrained—who will hold the line if the frontier erupts?

sentences.zh: 不如留舊兵畢獲，等級遣還。

translations.literal: Better to keep the old troops until harvest is finished and send them back by turns according to seniority.
translations.idiomatic: Better to let the veterans finish the harvest and send them home in orderly rotation.

sentences.zh: 仁軌當留，未可去。」

translations.literal: Rengui ought to remain; he must not leave.
translations.idiomatic: As for Rengui, he should stay—not leave now.

sentences.zh: 仁願不可，曰：「吾但知准詔耳。」

translations.literal: Renyuan would not agree and said, "I only know to follow the edict."
translations.idiomatic: Renyuan refused: "I have only to obey the edict."

sentences.zh: 仁軌曰：「不然。

translations.literal: Rengui said, "That is not so.
translations.idiomatic: Rengui insisted otherwise.

sentences.zh: 苟利國家，知無不為，臣之節也。」

translations.literal: If it benefits the state, knowing one must act without fail—that is a subject's duty."
translations.idiomatic: A loyal minister does whatever serves the realm without waiting to be told.

sentences.zh: 因陳便宜，願留屯。

translations.literal: He therefore set forth what was expedient and wished to remain on garrison duty.
translations.idiomatic: He laid out a practical alternative and petitioned to remain with the garrison.

sentences.zh: 詔可。

translations.literal: An edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor granted his request.

sentences.zh: 由是以仁願為不忠。

translations.literal: For this reason Rengui considered Renyuan disloyal.
translations.idiomatic: Rengui thereafter judged Renyuan disloyal to the state's interests.

sentences.zh: 始，仁軌任帶方州，謂人曰：「天將富貴此翁邪！」

translations.literal: At the beginning, when Rengui took office in Daifang Prefecture, he told someone, "Heaven is about to enrich and ennoble this old man!
translations.idiomatic: When Rengui first took office in Daifang, he told an associate, "Heaven means to make this old man rich and honored!

sentences.zh: 乃請所頒曆及宗廟諱，或問其故，答曰：「當削平遼海，頒示本朝正朔。」

translations.literal: He then requested a copy of the issued calendar and the taboo names of the ancestral temples; when someone asked the reason, he answered, "I shall level the Liaodong seas and proclaim our court's correct calendar."
translations.idiomatic: He requested the official calendar and the imperial taboo names; asked why, he said he intended to pacify Liaodong and impose the Tang calendar there.

sentences.zh: 卒皆如言。

translations.literal: In the end all came to pass as he had said.
translations.idiomatic: In the end everything happened exactly as he had predicted.

sentences.zh: 及封泰山，仁軌乃率新羅、百濟、儋羅、倭四國酋長赴會。

translations.literal: When Mount Tai was enfeoffed, Rengui then led the chieftains of the four states Silla, Baekje, Tamna, and Wa to the assembly.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor performed the Fengshan rites at Mount Tai, Rengui brought chieftains from Silla, Baekje, Tamna, and Japan to attend.

sentences.zh: 天子大悅，擢為大司憲。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven was greatly pleased and promoted him to grand minister of justice.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was delighted and promoted him to grand censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 遷右相，兼檢校太子左中護。

translations.literal: He was transferred to right chancellor and concurrently made acting protector of the crown prince's left guard.
translations.idiomatic: He was made chief minister of the right and acting protector of the crown prince's left guard.

sentences.zh: 累功封樂城縣男。

translations.literal: Accumulating merit, he was enfeoffed as Baron of Lecheng County.
translations.idiomatic: For accumulated merits he was ennobled as Baron of Lecheng.

sentences.zh: 總章元年，為熊津道安撫大使，兼浿江道總管，副李勣討高麗，平之。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zongzhang, he served as pacification commissioner of the Xiongjin Circuit and concurrently overall commander of the Peijiang Circuit, assisting Li Ji in campaigning against Goguryeo and pacifying it.
translations.idiomatic: In 668 he served as Xiongjin pacification commissioner and Peijiang military governor, assisting Li Ji in the conquest of Goguryeo.

sentences.zh: 以疾辭位，進金紫光祿大夫，聽致仕。

translations.literal: Illness made him resign his post; he was advanced to grand master of the golden girdle and purple rank and permitted to retire.
translations.idiomatic: Ill health forced his resignation; he was granted the rank of Grand Master of the Golden Girdle and allowed to retire.

sentences.zh: 俄召為隴州刺史，拜太子左庶子、同中書門下三品，監脩國史。

translations.literal: Soon he was summoned as prefect of Long Prefecture, appointed left attendant of the crown prince and of third grade together with the Secretariat and Chancellery, and overseer of the compilation of the national history.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon recalled as Longzhou prefect, then appointed left tutor to the crown prince with third-rank ministerial status and oversight of the national history project.

sentences.zh: 咸亨五年，為雞林道大總管，東伐新羅。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Xianheng, he served as grand overall commander of the Jilin Circuit and campaigned east against Silla.
translations.idiomatic: In 674 he became overall commander of the Jilin Circuit and marched east against Silla.

sentences.zh: 仁軌率兵絕瓠蘆河，攻大鎮七重城，破之。

translations.literal: Rengui led troops across the Hulu River, attacked the great fortress Qichong, and broke it.
translations.idiomatic: Rengui crossed the Hulu River, assaulted the major stronghold of Qichong, and took it.

sentences.zh: 進爵為公，子及兄子授上柱國者三人，州党榮之，號所居為「樂城鄉三柱裏」。

translations.literal: His noble rank was advanced to duke; three persons among his sons and brother's sons received the supreme pillar of state rank; the district honored him and called where he lived "Three Pillar Hamlet" in Lecheng Township.
translations.idiomatic: He was elevated to duke; three of his sons and nephews received the supreme merit rank; neighbors honored his household as "Three-Pillar Lane" in Lecheng Township.

sentences.zh: 俄拜尚書左僕射兼太子賓客，仍知政事。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed left vice director of the Department of State Affairs and concurrently guest of the crown prince, still participating in state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward he was named left vice minister of the Secretariat, also serving as adviser to the crown prince, and remained in active governance.

sentences.zh: 吐蕃入寇，命為洮河道行軍鎮守大使。

translations.literal: When Tibet invaded, he was appointed mobile pacification commissioner of the Taohu Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: When the Tibetans raided the frontier, he was named mobile defense commissioner of the Taohu Circuit.

sentences.zh: 永隆二年，加太子少傅。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yonglong, he was given the additional title of junior tutor to the crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: In 681 he was also made junior tutor to the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 數乞骸骨，聽解左僕射。

translations.literal: Repeatedly he begged to resign his bones; he was permitted to relinquish the post of left vice director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly petitioned to retire; the emperor allowed him to step down as left vice minister of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 帝幸東都，太子監國，詔仁軌與裴炎、薛元超留輔。

translations.literal: The emperor visited the eastern capital; the crown prince supervised the realm; an edict ordered Rengui, Pei Yan, and Xue Yuanchao to remain as assistants.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor went to Luoyang and the crown prince remained in Chang'an as regent, Rengui was ordered to stay behind with Pei Yan and Xue Yuanchao to assist him.

sentences.zh: 及太子赴東都，又詔太孫重照留守，仁軌副之。

translations.literal: When the crown prince went to the eastern capital, an edict again left the imperial grandson Chongzhao to hold the capital, with Rengui as his deputy.
translations.idiomatic: When the crown prince later joined the emperor at Luoyang, the edict left the emperor's grandson Chongzhao in charge of Chang'an, with Rengui as his deputy.

sentences.zh: 武后臨朝，復拜左僕射。

translations.literal: When Empress Wu presided over the court, he was again appointed left vice director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: After Empress Wu took control of government, he was reappointed left vice minister of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 太孫廢，仁軌專知留守事。

translations.literal: When the imperial grandson was deposed, Rengui alone handled the duties of holding the capital.
translations.idiomatic: After Chongzhao was deposed, Rengui alone directed affairs in the capital.

sentences.zh: 上疏辭疾，因陳呂後、祿、產禍敗事以規後，後遣武承嗣齎璽書慰勉。

translations.literal: He submitted a memorial pleading illness and, citing the disasters brought by Empress Lü, Lü Lu, and Lü Chan, admonished the empress; she sent Wu Chengsi bearing an imperial letter of consolation and encouragement.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized claiming illness and, pointing to how Empress Lü and her kin Lü Lu and Lü Chan had brought ruin upon themselves, cautioned Empress Wu; she sent Wu Chengsi with an imperial letter of reassurance.

sentences.zh: 改文昌左相、同鳳閣鸞台三品。

translations.literal: His title was changed to left chancellor of Wenchang and third grade together with the Phoenix Pavilion and Crane Platform.
translations.idiomatic: He was renamed left chief minister of Wenchang, with third-rank standing equal to the Phoenix Pavilion and Crane Platform offices.

sentences.zh: 卒年八十五。

translations.literal: He died at the age of eighty-five.
translations.idiomatic: He died at eighty-five.

sentences.zh: 詔百官赴哭，冊贈開府儀同三司、并州大都督，陪葬乾陵。

translations.literal: An edict ordered all officials to attend the mourning; posthumously he was enfeoffed as grand master of splendid appearance with ceremony equal to the Three Excellencies and as great protector of Bing Prefecture, and buried with honor at Qianling.
translations.idiomatic: Officials were ordered to attend the funeral rites; posthumously he received the titles of Grand Master of the Palace and governor-general of Bingzhou, and was buried beside the emperor at Qianling.

sentences.zh: 賜其家實封三百戶。

translations.literal: His family was granted three hundred households of perpetual noble income.
translations.idiomatic: His household received a permanent fief of three hundred taxpaying households.

sentences.zh: 仁軌雖貴顯，不自矜踞，接舊故如布衣時。

translations.literal: Although Rengui had risen to nobility and prominence, he did not pride himself or stand on ceremony; toward old friends he was as in his days wearing plain cloth.
translations.idiomatic: Though he had risen to the highest rank, Rengui never put on airs; he treated old friends exactly as he had when he was a common clerk.

sentences.zh: 嘗為御史袁異式所劾，慢辱之，肋使引決。

translations.literal: Once he was impeached by censor Yuan Yishi, who insulted and humiliated him and forced him to commit suicide.
translations.idiomatic: A censor named Yuan Yishi once impeached him, humiliated him, and tried to drive him to take his own life.

sentences.zh: 及拜大司憲，異式尚在台，不自安，因醉以情自解。

translations.literal: When he was appointed grand minister of justice, Yishi was still in the censorate and felt ill at ease; drunk, he explained himself from the heart.
translations.idiomatic: When Rengui became grand censor-in-chief, Yishi still served on the censorate staff and could not feel secure; one night, drunk, he poured out his fears.

sentences.zh: 仁軌持觴曰：「所不與公者，有如此觴。」

translations.literal: Rengui raised a cup and said, "What I would not share with you, sir, is like this cup.
translations.idiomatic: Rengui raised his goblet and said, "There is only one thing I would deny you—and it is this cup itself.

sentences.zh: 後既執政，薦為司元大夫。

translations.literal: Later, once he held power, he recommended him as grand master of the directorate of seasons.
translations.idiomatic: Later, once he held real power, he recommended Yishi for promotion to grand master of the directorate of seasons.

sentences.zh: 然宦由州縣至宰輔，善致聲譽，得吏下歡心。

translations.literal: Yet from county and prefecture posts to chief minister, he was skilled at winning reputation and gained the affection of officials beneath him.
translations.idiomatic: From county magistrate to chief minister, he had always known how to win a good name and keep subordinates devoted to him.

sentences.zh: 及鎮洮河，奏請機急，多為中書令李敬玄抑卻，仁軌乃表敬玄為帥以代己，果覆其眾。

translations.literal: When he guarded the Taohu frontier, his urgent memorials were mostly blocked by chief minister of the Secretariat Li Jingxuan; Rengui then memorialized to have Jingxuan replace him as commander, and Jingxuan indeed suffered defeat with his army.
translations.idiomatic: While commanding on the Taohu frontier, his urgent petitions were often blocked by chief minister Li Jingxuan; Rengui then recommended that Jingxuan replace him as commander—and Jingxuan's army was duly crushed.

sentences.zh: 裴炎下獄，仁軌方留守京師，郎將姜嗣宗以使來，因語炎事，且曰：「炎異于常久矣。」

translations.literal: When Pei Yan was thrown into prison, Rengui was just holding the capital; commandant Jiang Sizong came on a mission and spoke of Yan's affair, saying, "Yan has been acting oddly for a long time.
translations.idiomatic: While Pei Yan languished in prison and Rengui was holding Chang'an, commandant Jiang Sizong arrived on embassy business and spoke of the case, remarking, "Yan has been acting strangely for some time.

sentences.zh: 仁軌曰：「使人知邪？」

translations.literal: Rengui said, "Did the emissary know?"
translations.idiomatic: Rengui asked, "So the envoy knew?"

translations.literal: He said, "I knew."
translations.idiomatic: I did," Sizong replied.

sentences.zh: 及還，表嗣宗知炎反狀不告。

translations.literal: When he returned, Rengui memorialized that Sizong knew of Yan's treason and did not report it.
translations.idiomatic: When Sizong departed, Rengui memorialized that he had known of Yan's treason and kept silent.

sentences.zh: 武后怒，拉殺之。

translations.literal: Empress Wu was furious and had him strangled to death.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wu flew into a rage and had him strangled.

sentences.zh: 子浚，官太子舍人。

translations.literal: His son Jun served as attendant of the crown prince's household.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jun held the post of attendant in the crown prince's household.

sentences.zh: 垂拱中，為酷吏所殺。

translations.literal: During the Chuigong era, he was killed by cruel officials.
translations.idiomatic: During the Chuigong years he was murdered by the empress's inquisitors.

sentences.zh: 中宗即位，以仁軌有東宮舊，再贈司空。

translations.literal: When Zhongzong took the throne, because Rengui had old ties to the eastern palace, he was posthumously enfeoffed again as minister of works.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhongzong came to the throne, he posthumously honored Rengui again as minister of works, remembering his service to the crown prince.

sentences.zh: 浚子晃，開元中，為給事中，表請立碑，追諡曰文獻。

translations.literal: Jun's son Huang, during the Kaiyuan era, served as attendant censor; he memorialized to erect a stele and received the posthumous title Literary Exemplar.
translations.idiomatic: Jun's grandson Huang, a memorial drafter during the Kaiyuan reign, petitioned for a commemorative stele; Rengui was given the posthumous title Duke of Literary Merit.

sentences.zh: 裴行儉

translations.literal: Pei Xingjian
translations.idiomatic: Pei Xingjian

sentences.zh: 裴行儉，字守約，絳州聞喜人。

translations.literal: Pei Xingjian, style name Shouyue, was a native of Wenxi in Jiang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Xingjian, courtesy name Shouyue, came from Wenxi in Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 父仁基，隋光祿大夫，自王世充所謀歸國，被害。

translations.literal: His father Renji, grand master for splendid food in Sui, plotted to return to the Tang from Wang Shichong's camp and was killed.
translations.idiomatic: His father Renji, a Sui grand master of splendid provisions, had plotted to defect from Wang Shichong to the Tang and was executed for it.

sentences.zh: 贈原州都督，諡曰忠。

translations.literal: Posthumously he was made protector of Yuan Prefecture; his posthumous title was Loyal.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously Renji was made governor of Yuanzhou and given the posthumous name Loyal.

sentences.zh: 行儉幼引廕補弘文生。

translations.literal: In youth Xingjian entered by inherited privilege as a student of the Palace Academy for Literary Brilliance.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth Xingjian entered imperial service by inherited privilege as a student of the Palace Academy.

sentences.zh: 貞觀中，舉明經，調左屯衛倉曹參軍。

translations.literal: During Zhenguan he passed the classics examination and was appointed warehouse adjutant of the Left Garrison Guard.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhenguan reign he passed the classics examination and became warehouse secretary of the Left Garrison Guard.

sentences.zh: 時蘇定方為大將軍，謂曰：「吾用兵，世無可教者，今子也賢。」

translations.literal: At that time Su Dingfang was grand general; he said, "In military use I have no one in the world to teach; today you alone are worthy.
translations.idiomatic: Su Dingfang, then grand general, told him, "In all my campaigns I have found no one worth teaching—until now. You alone are worthy of my methods.

sentences.zh: 乃盡畀以術。

translations.literal: He then entrusted him with all his art.
translations.idiomatic: And he taught Xingjian everything he knew.

sentences.zh: 遷長安令。

translations.literal: He was transferred to magistrate of Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to magistrate of Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 高宗將立武昭儀，行儉以為國家憂從此始，與長孫無忌、褚遂良秘議，大理袁公瑜擿語昭儀母，左除西州都督府長史。

translations.literal: When Gaozong was about to install Lady Wu as consort Zhao, Xingjian held that national calamity began here; he secretly deliberated with Zhangsun Wuji and Chu Suiliang; Censor Yuan Gongyu of the Court of Judicial Review revealed the talk to her mother, and Xingjian was demoted and sent out as chief adjutant of the Protectorate General of Xizhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozong prepared to elevate Lady Wu as empress, Xingjian warned that national misfortune would begin there; he conferred secretly with Zhangsun Wuji and Chu Suiliang until Yuan Gongyu of the judicial review court betrayed the plot to Lady Wu's mother, and Xingjian was banished to serve as chief secretary in the Protectorate General of Xizhou.

sentences.zh: 麟德二年，擢累安西都護，西域諸國多慕義歸附。

translations.literal: In the second year of Linde, through successive promotions he became protector-general of Anxi; many western regions states came in admiration of righteousness to submit.
translations.idiomatic: By 665 he had risen to protector-general of Anxi; most of the Western Region states willingly submitted to Tang rule.

sentences.zh: 召為司文少卿。

translations.literal: He was summoned as vice director of the Directorate of Literary Works.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to court as vice minister of the directorate of literary works.

sentences.zh: 遷吏部侍郎，與李敬玄、馬載同典選，有能名，時號「裴馬」。

translations.literal: He was transferred to vice director of the Ministry of Personnel; with Li Jingxuan and Ma Zai he jointly managed selection; he had a reputation for ability and the age called them "Pei and Ma."
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to vice minister of personnel, he shared control of appointments with Li Jingxuan and Ma Zai; their competence was so renowned that people called them "Pei and Ma."

sentences.zh: 行儉始設長名榜、銓注等法，又定州縣升降、資擬高下為故事。

translations.literal: Xingjian first established methods such as the long roster and appointment registers, and fixed rules for ranking prefectures and counties and for matching qualifications to posts.
translations.idiomatic: Xingjian introduced the long-name roster and review-and-posting procedures, and codified rules for ranking prefectures and counties and matching qualifications to office.

sentences.zh: 上元三年，吐蕃叛，出為洮州道左二軍總管，改秦州右軍，並受周王節度。

translations.literal: In the third year of Shangyuan, when Tibet rebelled, he went out as overall commander of the left second army of the Taozhou Circuit, then of the right army of Qin Prefecture, both under the Prince of Zhou's command.
translations.idiomatic: In 676, when Tibet rebelled, he was sent out as commander of the left second army on the Taozhou front, then of the right army at Qinzhou, both under the Prince of Zhou.

sentences.zh: 儀鳳二年，十姓可汗阿史那都支及李遮匐誘蕃落以動安西，與吐蕃連和，朝廷欲討之。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yifeng, Ashina Duzhi, khan of the Ten Surnames, and Li Zhefu incited tribal settlements to stir up Anxi and joined with Tibet; the court wished to campaign against them.
translations.idiomatic: In 677 the Ten-Clans khan Ashina Duzhi and Li Zhefu stirred up the border tribes against Anxi and allied with Tibet; the court prepared to strike.

sentences.zh: 行儉議曰：「吐蕃叛皛方熾，敬玄失律，審禮喪元，安可更為西方生事？

translations.literal: Xingjian submitted a proposal, saying, "The Tibetan rebellion in Bingfang burns fierce; Jingxuan violated discipline; Shenli lost his life—how can we raise fresh trouble in the west?
translations.idiomatic: Xingjian argued, "Tibetan revolt is raging on the Bing frontier, Li Jingxuan has already been routed, and Liu Shenli is dead—why stir up more trouble in the west?

sentences.zh: 今波斯王死，其子泥涅師質京師，有如遣使立之，即路出二蕃，若權以制事，可不勞而功也。」

translations.literal: Now the King of Persia is dead, and his son Nipuoshi is held hostage in the capital; if an envoy were sent to install him, the route passes through the two invaders; by seizing the moment to manage affairs, achievement may come without labor.
translations.idiomatic: The King of Persia is dead and his son Nipuoshi is held at court. Send an envoy to restore him, and the route runs straight through our two foes. Handle the moment shrewdly and we may win without a pitched battle.

sentences.zh: 帝因詔行儉冊送波斯王，且為安撫大食使。

translations.literal: The emperor therefore ordered Xingjian to enfeoff and escort the King of Persia, and also to serve as pacification commissioner to the Arabs.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor appointed Xingjian to invest the Persian prince and escort him home, with additional authority as commissioner for relations with the Arabs.

sentences.zh: 徑莫賀延磧，風礫晝冥，導者迷，將士饑乏。

translations.literal: They went straight across the Gobi of Mohe-yan; wind and gravel darkened the day; guides lost their way; officers and soldiers hungered and lacked supplies.
translations.idiomatic: Marching straight across the Mohe-yan desert, they were blinded by sandstorms, their guides lost their bearings, and officers and men grew hungry and exhausted.

sentences.zh: 行儉止營致祭，令曰：「水泉非遠。」

translations.literal: Xingjian halted the camp and performed sacrifice, ordering, "Springs are not far.
translations.idiomatic: Xingjian halted the march, performed a rite of invocation, and announced, "Water is near.

sentences.zh: 眾少安。

translations.literal: The army somewhat calmed.
translations.idiomatic: The troops took heart.

sentences.zh: 俄而雲徹風恬，行數百步，水草豐美，後來者莫識其處。

translations.literal: Soon clouds cleared and winds stilled; after going several hundred paces, grass and water were rich and fine; those who came later could not recognize the place.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the sky cleared and the wind fell still; a few hundred paces on they found lush grass and water—and those who followed could never find the spot again.

sentences.zh: 眾皆驚，以方漢貳師將軍。

translations.literal: All were astonished and compared him to the Han General of the Second Division.
translations.idiomatic: The army was awestruck, likening him to Li Guangli of Han.

sentences.zh: 至西州，諸蕃郊迎，行儉召豪亻桀千餘人自隨。

translations.literal: Reaching Xizhou, the various foreign peoples came out to the suburbs to welcome him; Xingjian summoned more than a thousand chieftains to follow him.
translations.idiomatic: At Xizhou the border peoples came out to greet him in the suburbs, and Xingjian took more than a thousand local chieftains into his retinue.

sentences.zh: 揚言「大熱，未可以進，宜駐軍須秋」。

translations.literal: He proclaimed, "Great heat—one must not advance yet; better to encamp and wait for autumn."
translations.idiomatic: He announced publicly that the heat was too severe for campaigning and that the army would remain encamped until autumn.

sentences.zh: 都支覘知之，不設備。

translations.literal: Duzhi learned of it through spying and made no preparations.
translations.idiomatic: Duzhi's spies reported this, and he relaxed his defenses.

sentences.zh: 行儉徐召四鎮酋長，偽約畋，謂曰：「吾念此樂未始忘，孰能從吾獵者？」

translations.literal: Xingjian slowly summoned the chieftains of the Four Garrisons, falsely inviting them to hunt, and said, "I have never forgotten this pleasure—who will hunt with me?
translations.idiomatic: Xingjian then summoned the chieftains of the Four Garrisons under the pretense of a hunting party and said, "I have never forgotten the joys of the hunt—who will join me?

sentences.zh: 於是子弟願從者萬人，乃陰勒部伍。

translations.literal: Thereupon youths and sons wishing to follow numbered ten thousand; he secretly mustered the ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Ten thousand of their young men volunteered to follow, and under cover of the hunt he drilled his forces.

sentences.zh: 數日，倍道而進，去都支帳十餘里，先遣其所親問安否，外若閒暇，非討襲者。

translations.literal: Several days later, marching at double speed, when still more than ten li from Duzhi's camp, he first sent his close associates to inquire after his health, outwardly as if at leisure—not as raiders.
translations.idiomatic: Several days later he doubled the pace of march. Still a dozen li from Duzhi's camp, he sent trusted envoys ahead with courteous greetings, as though on a social visit rather than a raid.

sentences.zh: 又使入趣召都支。

translations.literal: He also sent men in to urge Duzhi to come.
translations.idiomatic: He sent another messenger to summon Duzhi to his camp.

sentences.zh: 都支本與遮匐計，及秋拒使者，已而聞軍至，倉卒不知所出，率子弟五百余人詣營謁，遂擒之。

translations.literal: Duzhi had originally plotted with Zhefu to wait until autumn to refuse the envoy; then hearing the army had arrived, in haste he knew not what to do; leading more than five hundred sons and youths he came to the camp to pay respects, and was seized.
translations.idiomatic: Duzhi had planned with Zhefu to put off the Tang envoy until autumn; when news of the army's arrival reached him, he panicked, gathered five hundred kinsmen, and came to pay his respects—and was seized on the spot.

sentences.zh: 是日，傳契箭，召諸部酋長悉來請命，並執送碎葉城。

translations.literal: That day, passing the tally arrow, he summoned all the chieftains of the tribes to come and receive orders, seized them all, and sent them to Suyab.
translations.idiomatic: That same day he passed the tally arrow and summoned every tribal chieftain to submit; all were taken and sent to Suyab under guard.

sentences.zh: 簡精騎，約齎，襲遮匐。

translations.literal: Selecting elite horsemen with light baggage, he struck at Zhefu.
translations.idiomatic: He picked a force of crack cavalry, traveled light, and raced to attack Zhefu.

sentences.zh: 道獲遮匐使者，釋之，俾前往諭其主，並言都支已擒狀，遮匐乃降，悉俘至京師。

translations.literal: On the road he captured Zhefu's envoy, released him, and sent him ahead to persuade his master, also telling of Duzhi's capture; Zhefu then surrendered, and all were taken captive to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: On the road they captured one of Zhefu's envoys, freed him, and sent him ahead to tell his master that Duzhi was already a prisoner; Zhefu surrendered and was brought to the capital with his followers.

sentences.zh: 將吏為刻石碎葉城以紀功。

translations.literal: Officers and clerks carved stone at Suyab to record the achievement.
translations.idiomatic: His officers carved a commemorative stele at Suyab to mark the victory.

sentences.zh: 帝親勞宴，曰：「行儉提孤軍，深入萬里，兵不血刃而叛黨擒夷，可謂文武兼備矣，其兼授二職。」

translations.literal: The emperor personally feasted him in gratitude, saying, "Xingjian led a lone army deep ten thousand li, took rebels without bloodshed on the blade—truly civil and martial together; let him receive two posts at once.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor feasted him in person and said, "Xingjian led a lone force ten thousand li into enemy country and brought the rebels to heel without a bloody battle—a man of both literary and martial gifts. Grant him two offices at once.

sentences.zh: 即拜禮部尚書兼檢校右衛大將軍。

translations.literal: He was immediately appointed minister of rites and concurrently acting grand general of the right guard.
translations.idiomatic: He was immediately named minister of rites and acting grand general of the right guard.

sentences.zh: 詔露元年，突厥阿史德溫傅反，單于管二十四州叛應之，眾數十萬。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhaolu, Ashide Wenfu of the Turks rebelled; twenty-four prefectures under the Chanyu Protectorate rose in response; their numbers reached several hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: In 679 the Turk Ashide Wenfu rebelled; twenty-four prefectures under the Chanyu Protectorate joined him, gathering several hundred thousand men.

sentences.zh: 都護蕭嗣業討賊不克，死敗系踵。

translations.literal: Protector Xiao Siye campaigned against the bandits without success; deaths and defeats followed one after another.
translations.idiomatic: Protector-general Xiao Siye failed to suppress them; defeat followed defeat and the dead piled up.

sentences.zh: 詔行儉為定襄道行軍大總管討之。

translations.literal: An edict made Xingjian grand overall commander of the Dingxiang Circuit to campaign against them.
translations.idiomatic: Xingjian was appointed grand overall commander of the Dingxiang Circuit to destroy them.

sentences.zh: 率太僕少卿李思文、營州都督周道務部兵十八萬，合西軍程務挺、東軍李文暕等，總三十余萬，旗幟亙千里，行儉鹹節制之。

translations.literal: He led Vice Minister of the Stud Li Siwen and Protector of Ying Prefecture Zhou Daowu with one hundred eighty thousand troops; together with the western army of Cheng Wuting and the eastern army of Li Wenhan and others, totaling more than three hundred thousand, banners stretching a thousand li—all placed under Xingjian's overall command.
translations.idiomatic: He led one hundred eighty thousand troops under Li Siwen and Zhou Daowu of Yingzhou, joined Cheng Wuting's western force and Li Wenhan's eastern force for more than three hundred thousand men; their banners stretched for a thousand li—and all came under Xingjian's command.

sentences.zh: 先是，嗣業饋糧，數為虜鈔，軍餒死。

translations.literal: Earlier, Siye had supplied grain but was repeatedly robbed by the enemy; the army starved and died.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Siye's grain convoys had been repeatedly ambushed; men starved to death in camp.

sentences.zh: 行儉曰：「以謀制敵可也。」

translations.literal: Xingjian said, "One may control the enemy by stratagem.
translations.idiomatic: Xingjian said, "We can beat them with a ruse.

sentences.zh: 因詐為糧車三百乘，車伏壯士五輩，齎齏陌刀、勁弩，以羸兵挽進，又伏精兵踵其後。

translations.literal: Thereupon he feigned three hundred grain carts; in each cart five strong men were hidden, carrying rations, long-handled infantry blades, and powerful crossbows; weak soldiers pulled them forward, and elite troops lay in ambush behind.
translations.idiomatic: He deployed three hundred decoy grain carts, each concealing five strongmen armed with dry rations, long-handled infantry blades, and heavy crossbows; sickly troops hauled them forward while elite soldiers lurked behind.

sentences.zh: 虜果掠車，羸兵走險。

translations.literal: The enemy indeed plundered the carts; the weak soldiers fled into defiles.
translations.idiomatic: The raiders took the bait and swarmed the carts; the decoy troops fled into the ravines.

sentences.zh: 賊驅就水草，解鞍牧馬。

translations.literal: The bandits drove toward water and grass, unslung saddles, and pastured horses.
translations.idiomatic: The Turks drove the carts to pasture, unsaddled their horses, and let them graze.

sentences.zh: 方取糧車中，而壯士突出，伏兵至，殺獲幾盡。

translations.literal: Just as they were taking from the grain carts, the strong men burst out, ambush troops arrived, and killed and captured nearly all.
translations.idiomatic: As they rummaged through the carts, the hidden soldiers leaped out; the ambush closed in and killed or captured nearly every man.

sentences.zh: 自是糧車無敢近者。

translations.literal: From this time none dared approach the grain carts.
translations.idiomatic: After that no raider dared come near a Tang grain convoy.

sentences.zh: 大軍次單于北，暮，已立營，塹壕既周，行儉更命徙營高岡。

translations.literal: The great army halted north of the Chanyu Protectorate; at dusk, camp already pitched and trenches complete, Xingjian again ordered the camp moved to a high ridge.
translations.idiomatic: The main army camped north of the Chanyu Protectorate. At dusk, with trenches dug and tents pitched, Xingjian suddenly ordered the camp moved to higher ground.

sentences.zh: 吏白：「士安堵，不可攏。」

translations.literal: Officials reported, "The soldiers are settled—it cannot be disturbed.
translations.idiomatic: His staff protested that the men were finally settled and should not be disturbed.

sentences.zh: 不聽，促徙之。

translations.literal: He did not listen and hurried the move.
translations.idiomatic: He refused to listen and drove them to break camp immediately.

sentences.zh: 比夜，風雨暴至，前占營所，水深丈餘，眾莫不駭歎，問何以知之，行儉曰：「自今第如我節制，毋問我所以知也。」

translations.literal: By night violent wind and rain suddenly came; the former campsite was flooded more than ten feet deep; none were not awestruck; asked how he knew, Xingjian said, "From now on simply follow my command—do not ask how I know."
translations.idiomatic: That night a violent storm flooded their former campsite waist-deep in water. The army was thunderstruck and asked how he had known; Xingjian said only, "Hereafter do as I command—and do not ask how I know."

sentences.zh: 賊拒黑山，數戰皆敗，行儉縱兵，前後殺虜不勝計。

translations.literal: The bandits held at Black Mountain; after several battles all ended in defeat; Xingjian unleashed his troops; before and after, slain enemy could not be counted.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels made their stand at Black Mountain and were beaten in battle after battle; Xingjian pressed the attack and the enemy dead mounted beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 偽可汗泥熟匐為其下所殺，持首來降；

translations.literal: The false khan Nishoufu was killed by his followers, who brought his head to surrender;
translations.idiomatic: The self-proclaimed khan Nishoufu was killed by his own followers, who brought his head to surrender;

sentences.zh: 又擒大首領奉職而還，餘黨走狼山。

translations.literal: The great chieftain Fengzhi was also captured and he returned; remaining bandits fled to Lang Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: Xingjian captured the chief leader Fengzhi and marched home; the remaining rebels fled to Lang Mountain.

sentences.zh: 行儉既還，阿史那伏念偽稱可汗，復與溫傅合。

translations.literal: After Xingjian had returned, Ashina Funician falsely styled himself khan and again joined with Wenfu.
translations.idiomatic: Hardly had Xingjian returned when Ashina Funician declared himself khan and reunited with Wenfu.

sentences.zh: 明年，行儉還總諸軍，屯代州之陘口，縱反間，說伏念，令與溫傅相貳。

translations.literal: The next year Xingjian again took overall command of all armies, encamped at the Pass of Daizhou, and spread counterintelligence, persuading Funician to turn against Wenfu.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he resumed overall command, encamped at the Daizhou pass, and sowed discord between Funician and Wenfu.

sentences.zh: 伏念懼，密送款，且請縛傅自效。

translations.literal: Funician was afraid, secretly sent submission, and asked to bind Wenfu to prove his loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: Funician grew fearful, sent secret overtures of surrender, and offered to bind Wenfu to prove his good faith.

sentences.zh: 行儉秘不布，密以聞。

translations.literal: Xingjian kept it secret and did not publish it, secretly reporting to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Xingjian kept this secret from the army and reported privately to the throne.

sentences.zh: 後數日，煙塵漲天而南，斥候惶駭，行儉曰：「此伏念執溫傅來降，非他也。

translations.literal: Several days later dust and smoke rose to the sky from the south; scouts were terrified; Xingjian said, "This is Funician bringing Wenfu bound to surrender—not another force.
translations.idiomatic: Days later a dust cloud rolled in from the south and scouts panicked; Xingjian said, "That is Funician bringing Wenfu in bonds—not an attack.

sentences.zh: 且受降如受敵。」

translations.literal: Moreover, receiving surrender is like receiving an enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Accepting a surrender is as perilous as accepting battle.

sentences.zh: 乃敕嚴備，遣單使往勞。

translations.literal: He therefore ordered strict preparations and sent a lone envoy to comfort them.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the camp on full alert and sent a single envoy to welcome them.

sentences.zh: 既而果然。

translations.literal: Soon it proved so indeed.
translations.idiomatic: And so it proved.

sentences.zh: 於是，突厥餘黨悉平。

translations.literal: Thereupon the remaining Turkic bandits were all pacified.
translations.idiomatic: With that the remaining Turkic rebels were finally crushed.

sentences.zh: 帝悅，遣戶部尚書崔知悌勞軍。

translations.literal: The emperor was pleased and sent Minister of Revenue Cui Zhidie to comfort the army.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was delighted and sent Cui Zhidie, minister of revenue, to congratulate the army.

sentences.zh: 初，行儉許伏念以不死，侍中裴炎害其功，建言：「伏念為程務挺、張虔勖肋逐，又磧北回紇逼之，計窮而降。」

translations.literal: At first Xingjian had promised Funician he would not die; Chief Minister Pei Yan, envious of his achievement, submitted a proposal, saying, "Funician was driven by Cheng Wuting and Zhang Qianxu and pressed by the northern Tiele beyond the desert; he surrendered when his plans were exhausted.
translations.idiomatic: Xingjian had promised Funician his life; but Chief Minister Pei Yan, jealous of his triumph, memorialized that Funician had been hounded into submission by Cheng Wuting and Zhang Qianxu and by the Tiele north of the desert, and had surrendered only in desperation.

sentences.zh: 卒斬伏念及溫傅於都市。

translations.literal: In the end Funician and Wenfu were executed in the capital market.
translations.idiomatic: In the end Funician and Wenfu were beheaded in the capital marketplace.

sentences.zh: 行儉之功不錄。

translations.literal: Xingjian's achievement went unrecorded.
translations.idiomatic: Xingjian's victory went entirely unrecorded in the official accounts.

sentences.zh: 封聞喜縣公。

translations.literal: He was enfeoffed as Duke of Wenxi County.
translations.idiomatic: He received only the title of Duke of Wenxi County.

sentences.zh: 行儉歎曰：「渾、浚之事，古今恥之。

translations.literal: Xingjian sighed and said, "The affair of Hun and Jun has been a shame through the ages.
translations.idiomatic: Xingjian sighed and said, "The affair of Hun and Jun has been despised through the ages.

sentences.zh: 但恐殺降則後無復來矣！」

translations.literal: Only I fear that if surrendering enemies are killed, none will ever come again!
translations.idiomatic: But I fear that if we kill those who surrender, none will ever come again!

sentences.zh: 遂稱疾不出。

translations.literal: Thereupon he claimed illness and did not go out.
translations.idiomatic: After that he pleaded illness and refused to appear at court.

sentences.zh: 永淳元年，十姓突厥車薄叛，復為金牙道大總管，未行卒，年六十四，贈幽州都督，諡曰獻。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yongchun, Che Bo of the Ten-Clan Turks rebelled; Xingjian was again made grand commander of the Jinya Circuit, but died before departing, at the age of sixty-four; posthumously he was made protector-general of You Prefecture, with the posthumous title Xian.
translations.idiomatic: In 682, when Che Bo of the Ten-Clan Turks rebelled, Xingjian was again named grand commander of the Jinya front—but he died before he could take the field, at sixty-four. Posthumously he was made governor-general of Youzhou and given the posthumous title Xian.

sentences.zh: 詔皇太子遣官護視家事，子孫能自立乃停。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the crown prince to send officials to oversee his household affairs; this was to continue only until his descendants could support themselves.
translations.idiomatic: An edict directed the crown prince to assign officials to manage the household until the descendants could fend for themselves.

sentences.zh: 中宗即位，再贈揚州大都督。

translations.literal: When Zhongzong took the throne, he was again posthumously enfeoffed as great protector of Yang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhongzong came to the throne, Xingjian was posthumously honored again as governor-general of Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 行儉工草隸，名家。

translations.literal: Xingjian was skilled in cursive and clerical script and was a celebrated master.
translations.idiomatic: Xingjian was a celebrated master of cursive and clerical calligraphy.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗以絹素詔寫《文選》，覽之，秘愛其法，賚物良厚。

translations.literal: The emperor once ordered him to copy the Wen Xuan on silk; on viewing it, he secretly admired his technique and rewarded him very generously.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once had him copy the Wen Xuan on silk; delighted with the hand, he heaped rich gifts upon him.

sentences.zh: 行儉每曰：「褚遂良非精筆佳墨，未嘗輒書，不擇筆墨而妍捷者，余與虞世南耳。」

translations.literal: Xingjian often said, "Chu Suiliang never wrote unless he had a fine brush and excellent ink; those who write beautifully and swiftly without choosing brush and ink—only Yu Shinan and I.
translations.idiomatic: Xingjian often said, "Chu Suiliang would not put brush to paper unless the ink and brush were perfect; as for those who write beautifully and swiftly no matter what they use—there are only Yu Shinan and myself.

sentences.zh: 所譔《選譜》、《草字雜體》數萬言。

translations.literal: He authored the Selection Criticism and Miscellany of Cursive Characters, tens of thousands of words.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote the Selection Criticism and Miscellany of Cursive Characters—works of tens of thousands of words.

sentences.zh: 又為營陣、部伍、料勝負、別器能等四十六訣，武后詔武承嗣就第取去，不復傳。

translations.literal: He also wrote forty-six maxims on encampments, formations, assessing victory and defeat, and distinguishing ability; Empress Wu ordered Wu Chengsi to fetch them from his house, and they were no longer transmitted.
translations.idiomatic: He also composed forty-six treatises on encampments, formations, judging battles, and appraising talent; Empress Wu had Wu Chengsi collect them from his home, and they were never circulated again.

sentences.zh: 行儉通陰陽、曆術，每戰，豫道勝日。

translations.literal: Xingjian understood yin-yang and calendrical arts; before each battle he foretold the day of victory.
translations.idiomatic: Xingjian mastered yin-yang lore and calendrical science and, before every battle, divined the day of victory.

sentences.zh: 善知人，在吏部時，見蘇味道、王抃，謂曰：「二君後皆掌銓衡。」

translations.literal: He was skilled at judging men; while at the Ministry of Personnel he saw Su Weidao and Wang Bian and said, "You two will later hold the balance of appointments.
translations.idiomatic: He had a gift for reading men. While serving in the Ministry of Personnel he met Su Weidao and Wang Bian and told them, "You will both one day control the scales of appointment.

sentences.zh: 李敬玄盛稱王勃、楊炯、盧照鄰、駱賓王之才，引示行儉，行儉曰：「士之致遠，先器識，後文藝。

translations.literal: Li Jingxuan greatly praised the talents of Wang Bo, Yang Jiong, Lu Zhaolin, and Luo Binwang and introduced them to Xingjian; Xingjian said, "For a gentleman to reach far, first comes disposition and insight, then literary art.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jingxuan lavishly praised the talents of Wang Bo, Yang Jiong, Lu Zhaolin, and Luo Binwang and brought them before Xingjian, who said, "A man who would go far must have judgment and breadth of mind before he has literary brilliance.

sentences.zh: 如勃等，雖有才，而浮躁衒露，豈享爵祿者哉？

translations.literal: Men like Bo, though talented, are restless and self-displaying—how could they enjoy rank and salary?
translations.idiomatic: Men like Bo may be clever, but they are restless and showy—how could such men long enjoy rank and emolument?

sentences.zh: 炯頗沉嘿，可至令長，餘皆不得其死。」

translations.literal: Jiong is rather silent and could reach the level of magistrate; the rest all died unnatural deaths."
translations.idiomatic: Jiong is comparatively reserved and might rise to county magistrate; the rest would all die before their time."

sentences.zh: 所引偏裨，若程務挺、張虔勖、崔智睟、王方翼、党金毘、劉敬同、郭待封、李多祚、黑齒常之，類為世名將，傔奏至刺史將軍者數十人。

translations.literal: The subordinate commanders he recommended—such as Cheng Wuting, Zhang Qianxu, Cui Zhicui, Wang Fangyi, Dang Jinbi, Liu Jingtong, Guo Daifeng, Li Duozuo, and Heichi Changzhi—became famous generals of the age; dozens were promoted through his memorials to prefect or general.
translations.idiomatic: The junior officers he singled out—Cheng Wuting, Zhang Qianxu, Cui Zhicui, Wang Fangyi, Dang Jinbi, Liu Jingtong, Guo Daifeng, Li Duozuo, Heichi Changzhi, and others—became the age's most celebrated commanders; dozens reached prefect or general on his recommendation alone.

sentences.zh: 嘗賜馬及珍鞍，令史私馳馬，馬蹶鞍壞，懼而逃。

translations.literal: Once he was given a horse and a fine saddle; a clerk privately rode the horse, the horse stumbled and the saddle was ruined, and the clerk fled in fear.
translations.idiomatic: Once, after he was given a horse and an exquisite saddle, a clerk took the horse out on his own; the horse stumbled, the saddle was ruined, and the clerk fled in terror.

sentences.zh: 行儉招還之，不加罪。

translations.literal: Xingjian summoned him back and did not punish him.
translations.idiomatic: Xingjian had him brought back and imposed no punishment.

sentences.zh: 初，平都支、遮匐，獲瑰寶不貲，蕃酋將士願觀焉，行儉因宴，遍出示坐者。

translations.literal: When he first pacified Duzhi and Zhefu, he obtained priceless treasures; tribal chiefs and officers wished to see them, and Xingjian, holding a banquet, displayed them all to those seated.
translations.idiomatic: After his first campaigns against Duzhi and Zhefu he had taken treasures beyond price; when tribal chiefs and officers asked to see them, he spread a feast and showed everything to his guests.

sentences.zh: 有瑪瑙盤廣二尺，文彩粲然，軍吏趨跌盤，碎，惶怖，叩頭流血。

translations.literal: There was an agate dish two feet wide, its patterns brilliantly colored; an army clerk hurried forward, tripped on the dish, and shattered it; terrified, he knocked his head until it bled.
translations.idiomatic: Among them was a two-foot agate dish of dazzling color; an army clerk hurried forward, stumbled against it, and smashed it to pieces. Terrified, he kowtowed until his forehead bled.

sentences.zh: 行儉笑曰：「爾非故也，何至是？」

translations.literal: Xingjian laughed and said, "You did not do it on purpose—why go to such lengths?
translations.idiomatic: Xingjian laughed and said, "You did not break it on purpose—why carry on like this?

sentences.zh: 色不少吝。

translations.literal: His expression showed not the least stinginess.
translations.idiomatic: Not a trace of regret crossed his face.

sentences.zh: 帝賜都支資產皿金三千餘物，橐駝馬牛稱是，行儉分給親故洎麾下，數日輒盡。

translations.literal: The emperor gave him more than three thousand items of Duzhi's assets—vessels, gold, and the like—along with camels, horses, and cattle in proportion; Xingjian divided them among kin, friends, and subordinates, and within days all was gone.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor granted him more than three thousand objects from Duzhi's estate—vessels, gold, and the like, with camels, horses, and cattle to match—and Xingjian distributed the whole lot among friends, relatives, and his command within days.

sentences.zh: 子 光庭

translations.literal: Son: Guangting
translations.idiomatic: His son Guangting

sentences.zh: 子光庭。

translations.literal: His son Guangting.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Guangting.

sentences.zh: 光庭字連城，早孤。

translations.literal: Guangting's style name was Liancheng; he was orphaned early.
translations.idiomatic: Guangting, courtesy name Liancheng, lost his father while still young.

sentences.zh: 母厙狄氏，有婦德，武后召入宮，為禦正，甚見親寵，光庭由是累遷太常丞。

translations.literal: His mother, surnamed Kudi, possessed womanly virtue; Empress Wu summoned her to the palace as director of moral instruction and greatly favored her; Guangting thereby rose in succession to vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: His mother, Lady Kudi, was a woman of exemplary conduct; Empress Wu brought her into the palace as director of moral instruction and treated her with great affection, and Guangting rose steadily until he became vice director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 以武三思婿，坐貶郢州司馬。

translations.literal: Because he was the son-in-law of Wu Sansi, he was demoted to military aide of E Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: As Wu Sansi's son-in-law, he was implicated and demoted to military aide at Ezhou.

sentences.zh: 開元中，擢兵部郎中、鴻臚少卿。

translations.literal: During the Kaiyuan era he was promoted to director in the Ministry of War and vice minister of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: During the Kaiyuan reign he was promoted to director in the Ministry of War and vice minister of court ceremonials.

sentences.zh: 性靜默，寡交遊，雖驟曆台省，人未之許，既而以職業稱，議者更推之。

translations.literal: His nature was quiet and reserved, with few social ties; though he rose rapidly through the central offices, people did not yet approve of him; once he distinguished himself in office, commentators revised their judgment.
translations.idiomatic: Quiet by nature and sparing in his friendships, he rose quickly through the capital ministries yet won little esteem at first; only when his competence became plain did opinion turn in his favor.

sentences.zh: 玄宗有事岱宗，中書令張說以天子東巡，京師空虛，恐夷狄乘間竊發，議欲加兵守邊，召光庭與謀，對曰：「封禪者，所以告成功也。

translations.literal: When Xuanzong planned rites at Mount Dai, Chief Minister Zhang Yue, fearing that with the Son of Heaven touring east the capital would be empty and barbarians might seize the moment to strike, proposed reinforcing the frontier; he summoned Guangting to consult, who replied, "Fengshan is how one announces success.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuanzong prepared to perform the fengshan rites at Mount Tai, Chief Minister Zhang Yue worried that with the emperor touring east Chang'an would lie empty and barbarians might exploit the moment; he proposed reinforcing the frontier and asked Guangting's counsel. Guangting answered, "The fengshan ceremony exists to proclaim success.

sentences.zh: 夫成功者，德無不被，人無不安，萬國無不懷。

translations.literal: Success means virtue reaches everywhere, no one is unsettled, and no realm fails to be drawn.
translations.idiomatic: Success means virtue that reaches every corner, people living in peace, and all nations looking to the throne.

sentences.zh: 今將告成而懼夷狄，非昭德也；

translations.literal: Now, about to announce success yet fearing barbarians—this is not displaying virtue;
translations.idiomatic: To proclaim success while fearing the barbarians is not to display virtue;

sentences.zh: 大興力役，用備不虞，非安人也；

translations.literal: to launch great corvée labor to guard against mishap is not settling the people;
translations.idiomatic: to mobilize vast labor in case of surprise is not to settle the people;

sentences.zh: 方謀會同，而阻戎心，非懷遠也。

translations.literal: just as one seeks universal gathering yet obstructs barbarian hearts—this is not embracing the distant.
translations.idiomatic: and to seek the gathering of all nations while blocking barbarian goodwill is not to win the distant realms.

sentences.zh: 此三者，名實乖矣。

translations.literal: In these three matters, name and reality diverge.
translations.idiomatic: In all three respects, word and deed would part company.

sentences.zh: 且諸蕃，突厥為大，贄幣往來，願修和好有年矣，若遣一使，召其大臣使赴行在，必欣然應命。

translations.literal: Moreover, among the various tribes the Turks are foremost; tribute and gifts have passed back and forth and a desire for good relations has endured for years; if we send one envoy to summon their ministers to the imperial camp, they will gladly obey.
translations.idiomatic: Among the frontier peoples the Turks are paramount; tribute has flowed both ways and they have sought peace for years. Send a single envoy to summon their ministers to the emperor's camp, and they will come gladly.

sentences.zh: 突厥受詔，則諸蕃君長必相率而來，我偃旗息鼓，不復事矣。」

translations.literal: Once the Turks accept the edict, the chieftains of all tribes will surely follow one after another; we may lower banners and silence drums, and have no further business.
translations.idiomatic: Once the Turks accept the imperial summons, every tribal leader will follow in their train; we can lower our banners and still our drums, and the matter will be settled.

sentences.zh: 說曰：「善，吾所不及。」

translations.literal: Yue said, "Excellent—beyond what I could reach."
translations.idiomatic: Yue said, "Well said—better counsel than I could offer."

sentences.zh: 因奏用其策，突厥果遣使來朝。

translations.literal: He therefore memorialized to adopt his plan, and the Turks indeed sent envoys to court.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized the throne to adopt the plan, and the Turks duly sent envoys to court.

sentences.zh: 東封還，遷兵部侍郎。

translations.literal: After returning from the eastern fengshan, he was promoted to vice minister of war.
translations.idiomatic: After the eastern fengshan rites he was promoted to vice minister of war.

sentences.zh: 久之，拜中書侍郎、同中書門下平章事，兼御史大夫。

translations.literal: After a long time he was appointed vice chief minister of the Secretariat, equal associate of the Secretariat and Chancellery, and also censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: In time he was made vice chief minister of the Secretariat, associate chief minister, and censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 遷黃門侍郎，拜侍中，兼吏部尚書、弘文館學士。

translations.literal: He was promoted to vice minister of the Chancellery, appointed chief minister, and also minister of personnel and scholar of the Hongwen Academy.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to vice minister of the Chancellery, was appointed chief minister, and also served as minister of personnel and Hanlin scholar.

sentences.zh: 撰《搖山往則》、《維城前軌》二篇獻之。

translations.literal: He wrote two essays, Lessons Drawn from Mount Yao and Former Tracks of the City Wall, and presented them.
translations.idiomatic: He composed two essays, Lessons Drawn from Mount Yao and Former Tracks of the City Wall, and presented them to the throne.

sentences.zh: 手制褒美，詔皇太子、諸王於光順門見光庭，謝所以規諷意。

translations.literal: The emperor's own hand praised them; an edict ordered the crown prince and princes to meet Guangting at Guangshun Gate and thank him for his admonitory intent.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor answered in his own hand with warm praise and ordered the crown prince and the princes to receive Guangting at Guangshun Gate and thank him for his counsel.

sentences.zh: 光庭又引壽安丞李融、拾遺張琪、著作佐郎司馬利賓直弘文館，撰《續春秋經傳》，自戰國訖隋，表請天子修經，光庭等作傳。

translations.literal: Guangting also brought Shou'an assistant magistrate Li Rong, remonstrance official Zhang Qi, and archive assistant Sima Libin to serve in the Hongwen Academy and compile the Continuation of the Spring and Autumn Classic and Commentary from the Warring States through Sui; he memorialized asking the Son of Heaven to write the classic while Guangting and the others wrote the commentary.
translations.idiomatic: Guangting also brought Li Rong, assistant magistrate of Shou'an, remonstrance official Zhang Qi, and archive assistant Sima Libin into the Hanlin Academy to compile a Continuation of the Spring and Autumn Classic and Commentary from the Warring States through Sui, proposing that the emperor compose the classic while he and his colleagues wrote the commentary.

sentences.zh: 書久不就。

translations.literal: The book long remained unfinished.
translations.idiomatic: The work was never completed.

sentences.zh: 時有建言唐應為金德者，中書令蕭嵩請百官普議。
