translations.literal: At the time some proposed that Tang should possess the virtue of Metal; Chief Minister Xiao Song asked all officials to discuss it broadly.
translations.idiomatic: Some then argued that the Tang should adopt the virtue of Metal; Chief Minister Xiao Song called for a general discussion among the officials.

sentences.zh: 光庭以唐符命表著天下久矣，不可改，亟奏罷之。

translations.literal: Guangting held that Tang's mandate had long been manifest throughout the realm and could not be changed; he urgently memorialized to stop it.
translations.idiomatic: Guangting held that the Tang mandate had been plain to the world for generations and could not be altered; he memorialized at once to quash the proposal.

sentences.zh: 二十年，封正平縣男。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year he was enfeoffed as Baron of Zhengping County.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year of Kaiyuan he was enfeoffed as Baron of Zhengping.

sentences.zh: 初，知星者言，上象變，不利大臣，請禳之。

translations.literal: Initially a star-reader said the celestial signs had changed to the disadvantage of great ministers and requested exorcism.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, an astrologer reported that a change in the heavens boded ill for high ministers and asked that rites of expiation be performed.

sentences.zh: 光庭曰：「使禍可禳而去，則福可祝而來也！」

translations.literal: Guangting said, "If misfortune can be exorcised away, then fortune can be prayed in!
translations.idiomatic: Guangting said, "If misfortune can be driven off by ritual, then fortune can be summoned by prayer!

sentences.zh: 論者以為知命。

translations.literal: Commentators considered him to understand fate.
translations.idiomatic: Commentators took this as proof that he understood destiny.

sentences.zh: 卒，年五十八，贈太師。

translations.literal: He died at the age of fifty-eight and was posthumously made Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: He died at fifty-eight and was posthumously honored as Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 初，吏部求人不以資考為限，所獎拔惟其才，往往得俊乂任之，士亦自奮。

translations.literal: Initially the Ministry of Personnel sought men without limiting itself to seniority and examination records; it rewarded and promoted only by talent, often obtaining outstanding men and appointing them, and scholars also exerted themselves.
translations.idiomatic: At first the Ministry of Personnel recruited without strict regard for seniority or service records, promoting men for talent alone; outstanding candidates were often placed in office, and scholars strove accordingly.

sentences.zh: 其後士人猥眾，專務趨競，銓品枉橈。

translations.literal: Later scholars swarmed in number, devoted themselves solely to rivalry, and evaluation was distorted.
translations.idiomatic: Later the ranks of candidates swelled, competition became the sole obsession, and appointments grew corrupt.

sentences.zh: 光庭懲之，因行儉長名榜，乃為循資格，無賢不肖，一據資考配擬；

translations.literal: Guangting punished this; following Xingjian's long-name roster, he instituted the seniority qualification system, so that regardless of worth or unworth, all assignments followed seniority and examination records;
translations.idiomatic: Guangting moved to curb the abuse. Drawing on Xingjian's long-name roster, he instituted the seniority qualification system: worthy or worthless alike, every posting followed service records alone;

sentences.zh: 又促選限盡正月。

translations.literal: He also shortened the selection deadline to the end of the first month.
translations.idiomatic: he also moved the selection deadline forward to the end of the first month.

sentences.zh: 任門下省主事閻麟之專主過官，凡麟之裁定，光庭輒然可，時語曰：「麟之口，光庭手。」

translations.literal: He put Yan Linzhi, a chief clerk of the Chancellery, in sole charge of pass-through appointments; whatever Yan decided, Guangting always approved; a saying of the time ran, "Yan's mouth, Guangting's hand.
translations.idiomatic: He put Yan Linzhi, a chief clerk of the Chancellery, in sole charge of clearing appointments; whatever Yan ruled, Guangting stamped approved. People said, "Yan's mouth, Guangting's hand.

sentences.zh: 素與蕭嵩輕重不平，及卒，嵩奏一切罷之，光庭所引，盡斥外官。

translations.literal: He had long been unequal in standing with Xiao Song; when he died, Song memorialized to abolish everything; all whom Guangting had appointed were expelled to outer posts.
translations.idiomatic: He and Xiao Song had long been rivals in influence. When Guangting died, Song memorialized to abolish the whole system and had every man Guangting had promoted driven out to provincial posts.

sentences.zh: 博士孫琬以其用循資格，非獎勸之誼，諡曰克平，時以為希嵩意。

translations.literal: Erudite Sun Wan, because he used the seniority qualification system and not the spirit of encouragement, gave the posthumous title Ke Ping; contemporaries thought this flattered Song's wishes.
translations.idiomatic: Erudite Sun Wan, judging that the seniority system was no way to reward merit, proposed the posthumous title Ke Ping; contemporaries saw this as currying favor with Xiao Song.

sentences.zh: 帝聞，特賜諡曰忠憲，詔中書令張九齡文其碑。

translations.literal: When the emperor heard, he specially granted the posthumous title Zhongxian and ordered Chief Minister Zhang Jiuling to compose the stele inscription.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor learned of this, he personally granted the posthumous title Loyal and Lawful and ordered Chief Minister Zhang Jiuling to write the epitaph.

sentences.zh: 子 稹

translations.literal: Son: Zhi
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhi

sentences.zh: 子稹，以廕仕，累遷起居郎。

translations.literal: His son Zhi entered office through yin privilege and rose in succession to diarist of the imperial bedchamber.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhi entered service by inherited privilege and rose to diarist of the imperial bedchamber.

sentences.zh: 開元末，壽王瑁以母寵，欲立為太子，稹陳申生、戾園禍以諫，玄宗改容謝之，詔授給事中。

translations.literal: Late in Kaiyuan, Prince Shou Li Mao, favored through his mother, was to be made crown prince; Zhi cited the disasters of Shen Sheng and Liyuan to remonstrate; Xuanzong changed expression and thanked him; an edict appointed him remonstrance officer.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Kaiyuan reign, Prince Shou Li Mao, favored through his mother, was nearly named crown prince; Zhi remonstrated by citing the fates of Shen Sheng and Prince Li. Xuanzong's face changed and he thanked him, then ordered him appointed remonstrance officer.

sentences.zh: 稹曰：「陛下絕招諫之路，為日滋久，今臣一言而荷殊寵，則言者將眾，何以錫之？」

translations.literal: Zhi said, "Your Majesty has blocked the path of remonstrance for ever longer days; now I speak one word and receive special favor—then remonstrators will be many; how will you reward them all?
translations.idiomatic: Zhi said, "Your Majesty has shut the door to counsel for too long. If a single word from me wins extraordinary favor, remonstrators will multiply—how will you reward them all?

sentences.zh: 帝善其讓，止不拜。

translations.literal: The emperor approved his modest refusal and did not appoint him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor admired his restraint and did not confer the post.

sentences.zh: 俄授祠部員外郎，卒。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed outer official of the sacrificial rites bureau and died.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was made outer official in the sacrificial rites bureau, and then died.

sentences.zh: 子倩，字容卿，曆信刺史我。

translations.literal: His son Qian, style name Rongqing, served as prefect of Xin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: His son Qian, courtesy name Rongqing, served as prefect of Xin.

sentences.zh: 勸民墾田二萬畝，以治行賜金紫服，代第五琦為度支郎中。

translations.literal: He urged the people to open twenty thousand mu of farmland; for his governance he was granted gold-and-purple robes; he replaced Di Wuqi as director of the finance branch.
translations.idiomatic: He urged the people to open twenty thousand mu of farmland; for his record in office he received gold-and-purple robes and replaced Di Wuqi as director of the finance branch.

sentences.zh: 卒，諡曰節。

translations.literal: He died; his posthumous title was Jie.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was given the posthumous title Jie.

sentences.zh: 子均。

translations.literal: His son Jun.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Jun.

sentences.zh: 玄孫 均

translations.literal: Great-great-grandson: Jun
translations.idiomatic: His great-great-grandson Jun

sentences.zh: 均字君齊，以明經為諸暨尉。

translations.literal: Jun's style name was Junqi; having passed the classics examination he became assistant magistrate of Zhuji.
translations.idiomatic: Jun, courtesy name Junqi, passed the classics examination and became assistant magistrate of Zhuji.

sentences.zh: 數從使府辟，硜硜以才顯。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly recruited by commissioner staffs and steadily distinguished himself by talent.
translations.idiomatic: Commissioners' staffs recruited him again and again, and he steadily made a name for himself by ability.

sentences.zh: 張建封鎮濠、壽，表團練判官。

translations.literal: When Zhang Jianfeng governed Hao and Shou, he recommended Jun as regimental training judge.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Jianfeng governed Hao and Shou, he recommended Jun as regimental training judge.

sentences.zh: 時李希烈以淮、蔡叛，建封扞賊，均參贊之。

translations.literal: At the time Li Xilie rebelled with Huai and Cai; Jianfeng resisted the bandits and Jun assisted him.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Xilie rebelled in Huai and Cai, Jianfeng held the rebels at bay and Jun served on his staff.

sentences.zh: 以勞加上柱國，襲正平縣男。

translations.literal: For his labors he was given the rank of superior pillar of state and inherited the barony of Zhengping County.
translations.idiomatic: For his service he was made superior pillar of state and inherited the barony of Zhengping.

sentences.zh: 遷累膳部郎中，擢荊南節度行軍司馬，就拜荊南節度使。

translations.literal: He rose through the ranks to director in the ministry of rites, was promoted to military adjutant of the Jingnan command, and then appointed military commissioner of Jingnan.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to director in the Ministry of Rites, was promoted to military adjutant of Jingnan, and then appointed military commissioner of Jingnan.

sentences.zh: 劉辟叛，先騷黔、巫，脅荊、楚，以固首尾，均發精甲三千，逆擊之，賊望風奔卻。

translations.literal: When Liu Pi rebelled, he first stirred up Qian and Wu and threatened Jing and Chu to secure his flanks; Jun sent three thousand elite troops to intercept him, and the bandits fled at sight of them.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Pi rebelled, he first stirred unrest in Qian and Wu and threatened Jing and Chu to secure his position; Jun sent three thousand elite troops against him, and the rebels broke and fled.

sentences.zh: 加檢校吏部尚書。

translations.literal: He was additionally made acting minister of personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He was given the additional title of acting minister of personnel.

sentences.zh: 初，均與崔太素俱事中人竇文場，太素嘗晨省文場，入臥內，自謂待己至厚，徐觀後榻有頻伸者，乃均也。

translations.literal: Initially Jun and Cui Taisu both served the eunuch Dou Wenchang; Taisu once visited Wenchang early in the morning and entered the inner chamber, thinking himself greatly favored; slowly he noticed someone stretching on the rear couch—it was Jun.
translations.idiomatic: Jun and Cui Taisu had both served the eunuch Dou Wenchang. Once Taisu called on Wenchang early in the morning and was admitted to the inner chamber, believing himself uniquely favored—until he noticed someone stretching on the couch behind him. It was Jun.

sentences.zh: 德宗以均任方鎮，欲遂相之，諫官李約上疏斥均為文場養子，不可汙台輔，乃止。

translations.literal: Dezong, because Jun held a frontier command, wished to make him chancellor; remonstrance official Li Yue submitted a memorial denouncing Jun as Wenchang's adopted son and unfit to stain the highest cabinet, and the appointment was stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Because Jun held a frontier command, Dezong meant to make him chief minister; but remonstrance official Li Yue memorialized that Jun was Wenchang's adopted son and unfit for the highest office, and the appointment was dropped.

sentences.zh: 元和三年，入為尚書右僕射，判度支。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yuanhe he entered the capital as right vice director of the Department of State Affairs and oversaw the finance branch.
translations.idiomatic: In 808 he entered the capital as right vice minister of the Secretariat and took charge of the finance branch.

sentences.zh: 旨唱、授桉、送印，皆尚書郎為之，文武四品五品、郎官、御史拜廷下，御史中丞、左右丞升階答拜，時以為禮太重。

translations.literal: Announcing the edict's purport, presenting the document desk, and delivering the seal were all done by directors; civil and military officials of the fourth and fifth ranks, directors, and censors bowed below the hall, while the vice censor-in-chief and left and right assistants ascended the steps to return the bows; contemporaries thought the ceremony excessively heavy.
translations.idiomatic: Directors performed every step of the appointment ceremony—reading the edict, presenting the document desk, delivering the seal. Civil and military officials of the fourth and fifth ranks, directors, and censors bowed below the hall while the vice censor-in-chief and the left and right assistants mounted the steps to return the bows; many thought the ritual excessive.

sentences.zh: 俄檢校左僕射、同中書門下平章事，為山南東道節度使，累封郇國公。

translations.literal: Soon he was acting left vice director, equal associate of the Secretariat and Chancellery, military commissioner of the eastern Shannan Circuit, and cumulatively enfeoffed as Duke of Xun.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made acting left vice minister, associate chief minister, and military commissioner of eastern Shannan, and was cumulatively enfeoffed as Duke of Xun.

sentences.zh: 以財交權幸，任將相凡十餘年，荒縱無法度。

translations.literal: He used wealth to befriend the powerful and favored; he held general and minister posts for more than ten years, dissolute and without discipline.
translations.idiomatic: He bought favor with the powerful and held high civil and military office for more than a decade, living dissolutely and without restraint.

sentences.zh: 卒，年六十二，贈司空。

translations.literal: He died at the age of sixty-two and was posthumously made Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He died at sixty-two and was posthumously honored as minister of works.

sentences.zh: 婁師德

translations.literal: Lou Shide
translations.idiomatic: Lou Shide

sentences.zh: 婁師德，字宗仁，鄭州原武人。

translations.literal: Lou Shide, style name Zongren, was a native of Yuanwu in Zheng Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Lou Shide, courtesy name Zongren, came from Yuanwu in Zhengzhou.

sentences.zh: 第進士，調江都尉。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination and was appointed assistant magistrate of Jiangdu.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination and was appointed assistant magistrate of Jiangdu.

sentences.zh: 揚州長史盧承業異之，曰：「子，台輔器也，當以子孫相諉，詎論僚吏哉？」

translations.literal: Yangzhou chief administrator Lu Chengye was impressed and said, "You, sir, are material for the highest cabinet; one should point you out to one's descendants—how speak merely of a colleague?"
translations.idiomatic: Lu Chengye, chief administrator of Yangzhou, was struck by him and said, "You, sir, are destined for the highest office; one should commend you to one's descendants—not speak of you as a mere colleague."

sentences.zh: 上元初，為監察御史。

translations.literal: Early in Shangyuan he was appointed supervising censor.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Shangyuan reign he was appointed supervising censor.

sentences.zh: 會吐蕃盜邊，劉審禮戰沒，師德奉使收敗亡於洮河，因使吐蕃。

translations.literal: When Tibet raided the border and Liu Shenli died in battle, Shide was sent on mission to gather the defeated and fugitives at Taohu and then sent as envoy to Tibet.
translations.idiomatic: When Tibet raided the frontier and Liu Shenli fell in battle, Shide was dispatched to gather the scattered survivors on the Taohu front and then sent as envoy to Tibet.

sentences.zh: 其首領論贊婆等自赤嶺操牛酒迎勞，師德喻國威信，開陳利害，虜為畏悅。

translations.literal: Their chieftain Lun Zanpo and others came from Chiling bearing oxen and wine to welcome and comfort him; Shide expounded the state's majesty and trust and explained benefits and harms; the barbarians were both awed and pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Their chieftain Lun Zanpo and others came from Chiling with oxen and wine to welcome him; Shide set forth the empire's majesty and good faith and explained what was to be gained and lost. The Tibetans were awed and won over.

sentences.zh: 後募猛士討吐蕃，乃自奮，戴紅抹額來應詔，高宗假朝散大夫，使從軍。

translations.literal: Later, when fierce warriors were recruited to campaign against Tibet, he himself stepped forward, wearing a red headband came to answer the edict; Gaozong temporarily made him Palace Gentleman for Dispersed Duty and sent him with the army.
translations.idiomatic: When the court later recruited fierce warriors for a campaign against Tibet, he volunteered, bound a red headband, and answered the call. Gaozong temporarily made him a palace gentleman and sent him with the army.

sentences.zh: 有功，遷殿中侍御史，兼河源軍司馬，並知營田事。

translations.literal: For merit he was promoted to palace censor, also made vice commander of the Heyuan Army, and jointly managed military colony affairs.
translations.idiomatic: For his service he was promoted to palace censor, made vice commander of the Heyuan Army, and put in charge of military colonies as well.

sentences.zh: 與虜戰白水潤，八遇八克。

translations.literal: He fought the barbarians at Baishui Stream; eight encounters, eight victories.
translations.idiomatic: He fought the enemy at Baishui Stream and won eight battles in eight engagements.

sentences.zh: 天授初，為左金吾將軍，檢校豐州都督。

translations.literal: Early in Tianshou he was made left Gold Crow general and acting protector-general of Feng Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Tianshou reign he was made left Gold Crow general and acting protector-general of Fengzhou.

sentences.zh: 衣皮袴，率士屯田，積谷數百萬，兵以饒給，無轉餉和糴之費。

translations.literal: Wearing leather trousers, he led troops in colony farming, accumulated millions of grain, the army was abundantly supplied, and there were no costs of transport or purchase.
translations.idiomatic: Wearing leather breeches, he led his men in colony farming and stored millions of measures of grain; the army was abundantly supplied without the cost of transport or market purchase.

sentences.zh: 武后降書勞之。

translations.literal: Empress Wu sent a descending letter to praise his labors.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wu sent an imperial letter commending his achievement.

sentences.zh: 長壽元年，召授夏官侍郎，判尚書事，進同鳳閣鸞台平章事。

translations.literal: In the first year of Changshou, summoned and appointed Vice Minister of Summer Offices, adjudicating Secretariat affairs, advanced to equal associate of Fengge and Luantai.
translations.idiomatic: In 692 he was summoned to court, made Vice Minister of Summer Affairs with charge of the Secretariat, and promoted to chief minister.

sentences.zh: 後嘗謂師德：「師在邊，必待營田，公不可以劬勞憚也。」

translations.literal: Later she once told Shide: "When you, sir, are on the border, you must rely on military colonies; you, sir, must not shrink from toil and fatigue.
translations.idiomatic: Later the empress told him: "On the frontier you must depend on colony farming—you must not shy from hard labor.

sentences.zh: 乃復以為河源、積石、懷遠軍及河、蘭、鄯、廓州檢校營田大使。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was again made acting commissioner of military colonies for the Heyuan, Jishi, and Huaiyuan armies and for He, Lan, Shan, and Kuo prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: He was then sent back out as acting commissioner of military colonies for the Heyuan, Jishi, and Huaiyuan Armies and for He, Lan, Shan, and Kuo prefectures.

sentences.zh: 入遷秋官尚書、原武縣男，改左肅政御史大夫，並知政事。

translations.literal: He entered court and was transferred to Minister of Autumn Offices and Baron of Yuanwu, changed to Left Censor-in-Chief of Sused Affairs, concurrently handling state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled to court, he was made Minister of Justice and Baron of Yuanwu, then Left Censor-in-Chief, handling affairs of state throughout.

sentences.zh: 證聖中，與王孝傑拒吐蕃於洮州，戰素羅汗山，敗績，貶原州員外司馬。

translations.literal: During Zhengsheng, with Wang Xiaojie he resisted Tibet at Taozhou, fought at Mount Siluo Khan, suffered defeat, and was demoted to outside assistant prefectural commander of Yuan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhengsheng era, he and Wang Xiaojie held Tibet at Taozhou and fought at Mount Siluo Khan; defeated, he was demoted to outside assistant commander of Yuan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 萬歲通天二年，入為鳳閣侍郎、同鳳閣鸞台平章事。

translations.literal: In the second year of Wansui Tongtian, he entered court as Vice Minister of Fengge, equal associate of Fengge and Luantai.
translations.idiomatic: In 696 he returned to court as Vice Minister of Fengge and chief minister.

sentences.zh: 後與武懿宗、狄仁傑分道撫定河北，進納言，更封譙縣子、隴右諸軍大使，復領營田。

translations.literal: Later with Wu Yizong and Di Renjie he pacified Hebei by separate routes, advanced to Court Counselor, was re-enfeoffed as Viscount of Qiao, made commissioner of the armies of Longyou, and again oversaw military colonies.
translations.idiomatic: He then joined Wu Yizong and Di Renjie in separate columns to pacify Hebei, rose to Court Counselor, was re-enfeoffed as Viscount of Qiao, made commissioner of the Longyou armies, and again took charge of military colonies.

sentences.zh: 聖曆三年，突厥入寇，詔檢校并州長史、天兵軍大總管。

translations.literal: In the third year of Shengli, the Turks invaded; he was ordered acting chief administrator of Bing Prefecture and grand commander of the Tianbing Army.
translations.idiomatic: In 699, when the Turks raided, he was ordered to serve as acting chief administrator of Bingzhou and grand commander of the Tianbing Army.

sentences.zh: 九月，卒於會州，年七十。

translations.literal: In the ninth month he died at Huizhou, aged seventy.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month he died at Huizhou, aged seventy.

sentences.zh: 贈幽州都督，諡曰貞，葬給往還儀仗。

translations.literal: Posthumously made protector-general of You Prefecture, posthumous name Zhen; funeral escort provided for the journey there and back.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously he was made governor-general of Youzhou and given the posthumous name Zhen; an honor guard was supplied for his funeral procession.

sentences.zh: 師德長八尺，方口博脣。

translations.literal: Shide was eight chi tall, with a square mouth and full lips.
translations.idiomatic: Shide stood eight chi tall, with a square mouth and heavy lips.

sentences.zh: 深沉有度量，人有忤己，輒遜以自免，不見容色。

translations.literal: Deep and reserved with great forbearance; when anyone crossed him, he would defer to avoid conflict and showed no change of countenance.
translations.idiomatic: Deep and even-tempered, he bore great forbearance: when anyone slighted him he would yield to avoid offense and never let it show on his face.

sentences.zh: 嘗與李昭德偕行，師德素豐碩，不能遽步，昭德遲之，恚曰：「為田舍子所留。」

translations.literal: Once he was walking with Li Zhaode; Shide was naturally stout and could not walk swiftly. Zhaode, kept waiting, angrily said: "Held up by some country bumpkin.
translations.idiomatic: Once when walking with Li Zhaode, Shide—naturally heavyset—could not keep pace. Zhaode, made to wait, snapped in irritation: "Delayed by some country lout.

sentences.zh: 師德笑曰：「吾不田舍，復在何人？」

translations.literal: Shide smiled and said: "If I'm not a country bumpkin, then who is?"
translations.idiomatic: Shide smiled and said: "If I'm not the country lout, who is?"

sentences.zh: 其弟守代州，辭之官，教之耐事。

translations.literal: His younger brother was taking leave for his post as prefect of Dai Prefecture; Shide instructed him in endurance.
translations.idiomatic: When his younger brother was leaving to take up the prefecture of Daizhou, Shide counseled him on forbearance.

sentences.zh: 弟曰：「人有唾面，潔之乃已。」

translations.literal: The brother said: "If someone spits in your face, wipe it clean and let it pass.
translations.idiomatic: The brother said: "If someone spits in your face, wipe it off and let the matter end.

sentences.zh: 師德曰：「未也。

translations.literal: Shide said: "Not enough.
translations.idiomatic: Shide said: "That won't do.

sentences.zh: 潔之，是違其怒，正使自幹耳。」

translations.literal: Wiping it would go against their anger; you should simply let it dry on its own."
translations.idiomatic: To wipe it is to defy their anger—better to let it dry of itself."

sentences.zh: 在夏官注選，選者就按閱簿。

translations.literal: While in Summer Offices assigning appointments, candidates came up to review the register.
translations.idiomatic: While serving in the Ministry of War assigning posts, candidates would come up to inspect the roster.

sentences.zh: 師德曰：「容我擇之可乎？」

translations.literal: Shide said: "May I choose for you?
translations.idiomatic: Shide would say: "May I choose one for you?

sentences.zh: 選者不去，乃灑筆曰：「墨汙爾！」

translations.literal: The candidate would not leave, so he splashed ink and said: "The ink has soiled you!"
translations.idiomatic: If a candidate would not budge, he would flick ink and say: "Look—it's stained you!"

sentences.zh: 狄仁傑未輔政，師德薦之，及同列，數擠令外使。

translations.literal: Before Di Renjie held chief ministerial rank, Shide recommended him; once they served together, Shide repeatedly pushed him out on missions abroad.
translations.idiomatic: Before Di Renjie entered the chancellery, Shide had recommended him; once they sat together at court, Shide repeatedly maneuvered to send him on missions abroad.

sentences.zh: 武后覺，問仁傑曰：「師德賢乎？」

translations.literal: Empress Wu noticed and asked Renjie: "Is Shide worthy?
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wu noticed and asked Renjie: "Is Shide a worthy man?

sentences.zh: 對曰：「為將謹守，賢則不知也。」

translations.literal: He replied: "As a general he is careful and dependable; as to worthiness, I do not know."
translations.idiomatic: He answered: "As a general he is cautious and reliable—as to virtue, I cannot say."

sentences.zh: 又問：「知人乎？」

translations.literal: She asked again: "Does he know men?"
translations.idiomatic: She asked again: "Does he know men?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「臣嘗同僚，未聞其知人也。」

translations.literal: He replied: "We were once colleagues; I have not heard that he knows men."
translations.idiomatic: He replied: "We served together once, but I never heard that he knew men."

sentences.zh: 後曰：「朕用卿，師德薦也，誠知人矣。」

translations.literal: She said: "I employed you because Shide recommended you—he truly knows men."
translations.idiomatic: She said: "I put you in office on Shide's recommendation. He knows men indeed."

sentences.zh: 出其奏，仁傑慚，已而歎曰：「婁公盛德，我為所容乃不知，吾不逮遠矣！」

translations.literal: She produced his memorial; Renjie was ashamed, then sighed: "Lord Lou's great virtue—I was sheltered by him and did not know it; I am far his inferior!"
translations.idiomatic: She produced the memorial; Renjie was mortified, then sighed: "Lord Lou's magnanimity—I was protected by him and never knew it. I fall far short of him!"

sentences.zh: 總邊要、為將相者三十年，恭勤樸忠，心無適莫，方酷吏殘鷙，人多不免，獨能以功名始終，與郝處俊相亞，世之言長者，稱婁、郝。

translations.literal: For thirty years he held frontier posts and served as general and minister, diligent, plain, and loyal, with no favoritism. When brutal censors predominated and many could not escape harm, he alone brought his career to an honorable end; ranked with Hao Chujun, the age's exemplars of the worthy called them Lou and Hao.
translations.idiomatic: For thirty years he commanded the frontier and held civil and military rank, plain-spirited, dutiful, and loyal, favoring none. When cruel officials held sway and few men escaped unscathed, he alone finished his career with honors intact—on a par with Hao Chujun; those who spoke of true elders in that age named Lou and Hao.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：「仁軌等以兵開定四夷，其勇無前，至奉上則瞿瞿若不及，行儉臨下以恕，師德寬厚，其能以功名始終者，蓋近乎勇於敢則殺，勇於不敢則活者邪！

translations.literal: The eulogy says: "Rengui and the others opened and settled the four barbarians by force—their courage unmatched—yet in serving their sovereign they were cautious as if barely adequate. Xingjian treated subordinates with forbearance; Shide was magnanimous. That they could see their careers through to the end perhaps approaches 'courage to dare brings death; courage not to dare brings life'!
translations.idiomatic: The appraisal reads: "Rengui and his peers opened the four frontiers by arms—their valor unmatched—yet before the throne they were watchful as men barely equal to the task. Xingjian was lenient toward those below; Shide was broad-minded. That they could preserve rank and reputation to the end perhaps comes close to Laozi's saying: to dare in courage is to kill; to dare in not daring is to live.
